nodes.label: asm-test documentation home
nodes.rationale: asm-test is a C-hosted unit-testing framework for assembly: call routines through the real ABI and assert on return values, registers, flags, and memory — filling the niche between whole-binary runners and assert-from-inside-asm approaches

nodes.label: Clean-room testing guide
nodes.rationale: asserts the bundled native library is the ONLY thing that could satisfy a dlopen binding's load — an import-worked smoke can be satisfied by an override/leaked build tree/brew copy and still print ok

nodes.label: Language bindings overview
nodes.rationale: ten bindings drive one flat C-ABI surface kept faithful by the layout manifest and a shared conformance corpus; libasmtest_emu is the superset (emulator + Keystone + Capstone)

nodes.label: Python binding (reference)
nodes.rationale: the reference binding — pure ctypes, packaged, pytest-native; reads struct layout from asmtest_abi.json and documents the Track D/E/F surface in full for the other bindings to mirror

nodes.label: Rust binding (extern + build script)
nodes.rationale: the no-GC native-path binding — #[repr(C)] mirrors match struct layout by construction, no crates.io deps

nodes.label: C++ binding (direct #include)
nodes.rationale: the C headers are C++-consumable as-is; asmtest.hpp is an optional RAII layer, and the emulator/assembler/disassembler tiers are opt-in build-time defines (-DASMTEST_ENABLE_*)

nodes.label: Zig binding (@cImport)
nodes.rationale: lowest-ceremony binding — consumes the C headers directly via @cImport, no separate binding layer; like C++ it gates tiers at build time but defaults them on

nodes.label: Installation guide
nodes.rationale: core has no third-party deps (the compiler also assembles the .s sources); optional tiers pull nasm/unicorn/keystone/capstone on demand, Keystone/Capstone via pinned source-build scripts (never distro)

nodes.label: Writing tests guide
nodes.rationale: a suite is foo.s + test_foo.c; TEST(...) auto-registers via a constructor so there is no list to maintain, and the Makefile auto-discovers the pair

nodes.label: ABI capture & registers guide
nodes.rationale: capture is post-return register state plus sentinel-based callee-saved checks; regs_t keeps ret/flags portable across ABIs, offsets _Static_assert-guarded so bindings can mirror them

nodes.label: Assertions guide (value/string/memory)
nodes.rationale: assertions longjmp back into the runner, failing only the current test; six families spread across ABI/FP/property/emulator pages

nodes.label: Benchmarks guide (cycles per call)
nodes.rationale: BENCH registers in a separate list from TEST, auto-calibrates a repeat count, reports min/median/mean via rdtsc/cntvct_el0 — real host cycles, not cross-arch comparable

nodes.label: Teaching with asm-test guide
nodes.rationale: the framework's primitives fit grading — fork isolation contains a student SIGSEGV/while(1), JUnit feeds Classroom, differential rubric items resist hard-coding, emulator runs cross-ISA student code on the x86-64 runner

nodes.label: Cross-system benchmarking guide
nodes.rationale: merges a host-independent deterministic instruction/model-cost metric with a feature/trace-completeness sweep into one normalized report; the repo is the benchmark database (golden emu counts + per-box history)

nodes.label: Disassembly guide (Capstone diagnostics)
nodes.rationale: diagnostic-only, optional Capstone-backed annotation of emulator faults/traces/coverage byte-offsets; self-skips to offset-only output when Capstone is absent

nodes.label: Emulator tier guide (Unicorn)
nodes.rationale: runs a routine inside a virtual CPU to preload registers/memory, single-step mid-routine, read the full register file, turn invalid accesses into precise fault data, and measure basic-block coverage; guests emulate on any host

nodes.label: Floating-point & SIMD guide
nodes.rationale: FP/vector capture paths (ASM_FCALLn/ASM_VCALLn/ASM_VCALL256n/ASM_SVCALL) marshal doubles/128-/256-bit/scalable vectors and capture the whole vector file; wide-vector capture is native-only (Unicorn doesn't execute AVX/AVX-512)

nodes.label: External-engine fuzzing shim guide
nodes.rationale: drives a guest routine with libFuzzer/AFL++ while feeding the emulator's block coverage as the feedback signal — the guest is raw code under Unicorn, so the harness writes an external coverage map by hand

nodes.label: Property/differential testing guide
nodes.rationale: the framework's signature capability — fuzz a routine against a C reference model over seeded inputs, report the first mismatch shrunk to a boundary value; seed fixed by default for reproducibility, ASMTEST_SEED to vary

nodes.label: Test runner guide (fork isolation)
nodes.rationale: each test runs in a fork()ed child under an alarm() timeout so a hang becomes a reported timeout and a crash a reported failure; the runner records nothing itself — it arms a directory and carries a producer's note

nodes.label: Native Win64 tier guide
nodes.rationale: captures/asserts the Microsoft x64 ABI on real x86-64 silicon without a Windows host — via ms_abi attribute or a PE under Wine; the runner port maps each POSIX primitive to a Win32 equivalent

nodes.label: Capture trampoline
nodes.rationale: the framework's differentiator — an assembly trampoline that seeds callee-saved sentinels, marshals args, performs the real call, and snapshots every GP register plus flags into regs_t, so a clobbered-then-restored register is still caught

nodes.label: In-line assembler (Keystone)
nodes.rationale: pass a routine as assembly text instead of a compiled address; multi-arch assemble-to-bytes (x86-64/arm64/riscv64/arm32); folded into the libasmtest_emu superset

nodes.label: Native tracing tier (DynamoRIO / NativeTrace)
nodes.rationale: traces host-native code in-process under DynamoRIO (libasmtest_drapp), dlopen'd at run time and self-skipping when absent; flaky under managed runtimes (CLR/JVM/V8) where in-process takeover can't cover background threads

nodes.label: Hardware / single-step tracing tier (HwTrace)
nodes.rationale: records the same asmtest_trace_t coverage from the real CPU; defaults to the EFLAGS.TF single-step backend so it traces live on any x86-64 Linux with no engine install, picking Intel PT / AMD LBR automatically on bare metal

nodes.label: Tier-2 assertions
nodes.rationale: idiomatic per-language assertion wrappers over the capture/emulator results (assert_ret, assert_abi_preserved, assert_no_fault, ...); nine of ten bindings ship them, Zig excepted

nodes.label: Shared conformance corpus
nodes.rationale: the single source of truth every binding replays and must reproduce (the same corpus.json the C reference emits), keeping the flat C-ABI surface faithful across ten languages

nodes.label: ABI layout manifest (asmtest_abi.json)
nodes.rationale: machine-readable struct layout the Python binding reads so it is automatically correct for whatever arch the lib was built for; C _Static_asserts guarantee it matches the real structs

nodes.label: Per-step register capture (emu_step_capture)
nodes.rationale: opt-in producer that snapshots the full register file before every executed instruction into a bounded, drop-accounted ring — the step-by-step register history a scrubber replays from; truncation is data, never a silent gap

nodes.label: Cross-arch emulator guests (x86-64/arm64/riscv64/arm32/win64)
nodes.rationale: all guests share one open/map/write/call shape over a single Unicorn engine; AArch64/RISC-V/ARM32 run raw bytes on an x86-64 host, and Win64 rides the x86-64 engine so its ABI is exercised without a Windows host

nodes.label: Instruction-capture depth ladder / trace-completeness metric
nodes.rationale: a ladder of loop/recursion rungs compares each backend's captured instruction count to the emulator's deterministic truth, exposing a fixed-window backend's ceiling (AMD LBR's 16-deep window) and native-auto's escalation that restores completeness

LBR+live-IBS tier moved from manual to the hwtrace-privileged-zen CI lane 2026-07-22.

Hard gate: host current_clocksource must read 'tsc' or macOS/KVM guests freeze under load (measured TSC warp at boot; no SMP/pin/-tsc-deadline combination survives — fix is a host reboot). CPU=Haswell-noTSX-IBRS, Ventura, one-time VNC install produces reusable disk.

nodes.rationale: The one Intel-PT validation CI cannot run: live whole-window capture + libipt decode, foreign-pid attach, per-tid hop, F5 PT-replay need bare-metal Intel PT silicon (VMs give no or heartbeat-only AUX). Validated live on Core i7-8559U; surfaced+fixed a code-image caller-fallback defect synthetic CI could never catch; managed multi-threaded PT path had a non-deterministic race.

nodes.rationale: Records what shipped for scoped tracing across all ten bindings via the single-step WEAK tier, and what stays hardware-gated: STRONG Intel PT live capture, CEILING AMD LBR live floor, per-thread PT/CoreSight AUX validation. §D3 out-of-process ptrace-stealth stepper is the hardware-free scope path for Zen 2 / Docker-on-Mac.

Second theme: AArch64 ABI-capture fidelity gaps. All 54 addressed.

nodes.rationale: Review of the asmtest_descent_t out-of-process descending ptrace tracer. 9 correctness/quality fixes (stale L3 watchdog flag aborting healthy L1/L2 traces, double-reaped fork tracee, hard step-cap returning OK, Capstone probe done 3x per step). Shadow-stack pop predicate and SP-sweep verified correct. D1/D2 (signal-frame SP-pop, tail-call keep-open) documented as live-path limitations.

nodes.rationale: Cross-check of 11 active plans: core framework + every tracing tier's software half shipped and CI-gated. Remaining work splits into unblocked backlog, hardware/silicon/privilege-blocked (Intel PT live, CoreSight board, Zen 3 BRS, AArch64 ptrace under qemu), and maintainer/credential actions (first real tag).

nodes.rationale: Empirical host-specific answer: native = core + emulator + macOS-Intel single-step live (87/0); Docker Linux = DynamoRIO + single-step/ptrace; impossible = AMD LBR (wrong vendor) and Intel PT live (Virtualization.framework hides the PMU even under --privileged, macOS has no PT interface). A native macOS PT kext is real-but-uneconomical research; single-step is the correct macOS-Intel tier.

nodes.label: AMD tracing review F1–F47 (2026-07-09, authoritative)
nodes.rationale: Adversarially re-verified AMD review. Central structural fact: the dev/CI host is Zen 2 (no LbrExtV2, no Zen 3 BRS), so every branch-stack path self-skips and the real exact path is single-step/block-step via trace_auto.c. Top items: use block-step in JIT lanes (F18), give the escalation ladder a rung discriminator (F22), struct_size on the options struct (F27), IBS-Op fallback for the survey (F6), don't return OK for an empty escalated trace (F24).

nodes.label: AMD tracing review — first pass 2026-07-09 (superseded)
nodes.rationale: First-pass AMD review, superseded same day by the F1–F47 edition. Notable recommendation §4.4: after a truncated AMD LBR result, try the BPF snapshot or MSR-direct path before falling to block-step (avoids the ~1000x block-step slowdown). §3.3: MSR-direct path leaks phantom speculative wrong-path edges because it constructs perf_branch_entry with zeroed flags.

nodes.label: Cross-architecture benchmarking design 2026-07-11
nodes.rationale: Two tiers: A = real-cycle per-host (native BENCH; cyc vs ticks never comparable across arches), B = architecture-agnostic dynamic instruction/block count via the emulator's insns_total, deterministic and host-independent. Key insight: insns_total lives in asmtest_trace_t which every trace backend fills, so the count metric rides the existing trace-parity substrate and its auto-resolution cascade for free.

nodes.label: Zen 2 hardware-tracing review — IBS is the one unused lever 2026-07-12
nodes.rationale: Empirical Zen 2 (Ryzen 9 4900HS) review: every exact hardware trace tier self-skips; IBS-Op is the one usable branch source and was completely unused. Refutes the AMD plan's Phase-7 privilege assumptions — user-only IBS needs no privilege (kernel swfilt makes exclude_kernel work at paranoid=2), and the branch target arrives in the perf record (reg[7] IbsBrTarget) with no MSR read. Ranked #1: build the IBS-Op statistical edge lane.
nodes.norm_label: zen 2 hardware-tracing review — ibs is the one unused lever 2026-07-12

nodes.label: Zen 5 privileged-capture findings — first live AMD LBR/IBS run 2026-07-12
nodes.rationale: First live AMD LbrExtV2 + IBS capture on Ryzen 9 9950X via CAP_PERFMON alone (no --privileged). Found + fixed a correctness bug: trace_call_auto's AMD-LBR rung mis-reported a freeze-on-PMI richest-in-region tail window as complete (6-of-77-instruction read, truncated=0, no escalation) because the exit-presence check was gated behind !freeze_available; now runs on every part.
nodes.norm_label: zen 5 privileged-capture findings — first live amd lbr/ibs run 2026-07-12

nodes.label: Block-step + emulator-replay value spike (F1) 2026-07-15
nodes.rationale: GO verdict. Block-step (PTRACE_SINGLEBLOCK, one stop per taken branch) + Unicorn replay of the straight-line interior seeded from real boundary GETREGS reconstructs a value trace byte-identical to true single-step (literal memcmp) while cutting in-region stops ~6x. Purity classifier flags syscall/rdtsc/cpuid/rdrand as impure→single-step fallback; a coherence canary drops divergence to truncated. Undefined-flag risk mapped.

nodes.label: Hardware data-watchpoint spike (F3) 2026-07-15
nodes.rationale: GO verdict. x86 debug registers in write/read-write mode (a one-field DR7 change on the existing execution-breakpoint path) answer 'who touched this field, with what value' at near-zero perturbation — victim ran at native speed between hits (±7% noise), ~2,000,000x fewer stops than single-step. Per-thread arming mandatory for live multi-threaded targets; R/W=11 traps loads but DR6 doesn't give direction (needs one-instruction decode). AArch64 NT_ARM_HW_WATCH analog sketched.

nodes.label: Intel PT backend (ASMTEST_HWTRACE_INTEL_PT)
nodes.rationale: TNT/TIP/PSB packets into the kernel AUX ring via perf_event_open, decoded by libipt; bare-metal Intel x86-64 only, out-of-band so recommended for JIT/GC managed runtimes. Ceiling = ring size.

nodes.label: AMD LBR backend (LbrExtV2, ASMTEST_HWTRACE_AMD_LBR)
nodes.rationale: Reconstructs the exact instruction/block stream from the 16-deep LbrExtV2 branch stack, delivered at a PMU sample; Zen 4+. 16-deep window lifted by Tier-B stitching; remaining ceiling is the perf data ring (data_size) plus PMI throttling. Faithfully marks a too-fast single-shot routine truncated.

nodes.label: ARM CoreSight backend (ASMTEST_HWTRACE_CORESIGHT)
nodes.rationale: ETM/ETE waypoints into the AUX ring, decoded by OpenCSD; documented scaffold that always self-skips pending a specific AArch64 board (Juno/Kria/Jetson/Pixel), prohibited in KVM guests.

nodes.label: Single-step backend (EFLAGS.TF → #DB → SIGTRAP)
nodes.rationale: The universal floor: same exact/complete offsets as Intel PT on any x86-64 Linux or macOS with no PMU/perf/privilege/decoder, no depth ceiling. Trade is exact-cheap vs exact-slow (~2 us/instruction) so it suits small registered routines, not whole-program tracing.

nodes.label: AMD IBS-Op statistical lane
nodes.rationale: Instruction-Based Sampling tags one retired op per window; a tagged taken branch carries source+target = a sampled from→to edge. Out-of-band, unprivileged (kernel swfilt at paranoid=2), works on every Zen incl. Zen 2 where exact backends self-skip. Fills its own asmtest_ibs_survey_t, never asmtest_trace_t — statistical, never exact; safe on a live JIT.

nodes.label: DynamoRIO software-DBI native-trace tier
nodes.rationale: Traces native in-process execution via DynamoRIO's BSD core API only (no drmgr/drwrap, avoiding LGPL). Linux/macOS x86-64. Cannot take over a JIT/GC runtime's background threads (Node/.NET self-skip), where hardware trace is the recommended backend.

nodes.label: Out-of-process ptrace single-step tracer (W2)
nodes.rationale: A tracer parent PTRACE_SINGLESTEPs a forked or attached tracee; same exact offsets without touching the target's signal disposition or code cache — the path for managed runtimes, on AMD, and the only single-step form on AArch64. Carries the foreign-JIT toolkit (/proc/maps, perf-maps, jitdump, run_to, code-image recorder) and call descent.

nodes.label: Block-step (PTRACE_SINGLEBLOCK)
nodes.rationale: One #DB per taken branch, reconstructing a byte-identical offset stream while stepping over call-outs at native speed — an order-of-magnitude fewer ptrace round-trips than per-instruction single-step. Must be probed functionally (hypervisors can mask DEBUGCTL.BTF). A rep-prefixed string op is reconstructed once → the block is marked truncated.

nodes.label: Unicorn emulator trace tier
nodes.rationale: Runs a routine's bytes in an isolated virtual CPU (x86-64/AArch64/RISC-V/ARM32), giving deterministic host-independent instruction/block counts, faults-as-data, and cross-ISA execution. The L0 value-trace oracle for the data-flow tier and the cross-check anchor for SDE.

nodes.label: MSR-direct LBR snapshot
nodes.rationale: Exact zero-interrupt Tier-A read of the 16-deep LbrExtV2 stack via /dev/cpu/N/msr; needs root/CAP_SYS_ADMIN + the msr module (self-hosted runners only). The kernel does not save/restore the stack across context switches, so eviction of early edges yields faithful truncation.

nodes.label: eBPF boundary LBR snapshot (branchsnap)
nodes.rationale: A hardware breakpoint at the region exit triggers a small eBPF program that reads the frozen 16-entry stack (bpf_get_branch_snapshot) — the deterministic fix for the too-fast single-shot routine the sampled path can only mark truncated. Needs CAP_BPF + BPF toolchain, Zen 4+, Linux >= 6.10; one frozen window, does not stitch past 16 branches.

nodes.label: Hardware data watchpoint (DR0-3 / NT_ARM_HW_WATCH)
nodes.rationale: asmspy --watch arms an x86-64 DR0-3 (or AArch64 NT_ARM_HW_WATCH) data watchpoint on a field in every thread and reports each toucher + value while the target runs at native speed between hits. 4 slots, per-thread, widths 1/2/4/8, self-skips where no watchpoint slots exist (qemu-user).

nodes.label: Intel SDE future-ISA emulation lane
nodes.rationale: Runs an unmodified suite binary under sde64 -future so routines using APX/AVX10.2/AMX/AVX-512-on-AVX2 get the full register/flag/memory/ABI assertion battery on any x86-64 host. Proves transparency via byte-identical native-vs-SDE TAP and a Unicorn cross-check; asserts up to emulation fidelity (architectural results, not timing).

nodes.label: Intel Pin probe-mode arg/return capture
nodes.rationale: A test/oracle-only data-flow producer: Pin splices a probe (a jump) at a routine's entry/exit and reads SysV arg/return registers + a pointed-to buffer at native speed, cross-checked against the ptrace single-step producer. x86-only; Pin is proprietary freeware, never linked into shipped libraries.

nodes.label: asmtest_trace_t shared trace shape
nodes.rationale: One result shape (ordered instruction offsets, distinct basic-block offsets, totals, a truncation bit) every trace backend fills, so a test switches backends without changing how it reads coverage. insns_total also rides as the cross-ISA benchmarking metric.

nodes.label: Complete-or-truncated fidelity contract
nodes.rationale: Every backend either emits a complete trace or flags asmtest_trace_t.truncated — a partial capture is never emitted as complete. The recovery idiom is dynamic fallback: re-resolve under CEILING_FREE. The 2026-07-02 review found this contract broken in essentially every backend.

nodes.label: AMD Tier-B window stitching
nodes.rationale: Splices overlapping 16-deep sample_period=1 windows into one gapless sequence, lifting the 16-branch ceiling; the remaining ceiling is the data ring plus PMI throttling. lbr_period spacing trades interrupts for reach but silently undercounts self-similar loops; a stitch gap yields faithful truncation.

nodes.label: asmtest_trace_call_auto cross-tier escalation cascade
nodes.rationale: Picks the most-faithful available backend (Intel PT > AMD LBR > single-step > CoreSight), detects truncated, and escalates to a ceiling-free rung. The AMD reviews flagged that the ladder reported all rungs as SINGLESTEP (needs a rung discriminator) and could return OK for an empty escalated trace.

nodes.label: Zen 2 silicon gate (IBS-only, no branch stack)
nodes.rationale: Zen 2 (family 17h) has no LbrExtV2 (Zen 4+) and no Zen 3 BRS, so every exact AMD branch-stack path self-skips; IBS-Op is the only hardware branch source, and the real exact path is single-step/block-step via trace_auto.c.
nodes.norm_label: zen 2 silicon gate (ibs-only, no branch stack)

nodes.label: Zen 4+ LbrExtV2 gate
nodes.rationale: The exact AMD LBR floor is Zen 4 LbrExtV2 (Zen 3 BRS exists in silicon but this tree never opens it). Live-validated on a Ryzen 9 9950X (Zen 5) via CAP_PERFMON.

nodes.label: Bare-metal Intel PT gate
nodes.rationale: A real control-flow AUX trace needs bare-metal Intel PT silicon; VMs/hypervisors (incl. Apple Virtualization.framework) hide the intel_pt PMU or give only a heartbeat stream, so live PT tests self-skip everywhere in the cloud. No GitHub-hosted bare-metal Intel PT box exists.

nodes.label: AArch64 CoreSight board gate
nodes.rationale: CoreSight self-hosted trace needs a specific AArch64 board (Juno/Kria/Jetson/Pixel) and is prohibited in KVM guests; the backend is a documented scaffold that always self-skips pending board access.

nodes.label: perf_event_paranoid / CAP_PERFMON gate
nodes.rationale: PT/AMD-LBR capture needs perf_event_paranoid lowered or CAP_PERFMON — a host knob the process cannot grant itself. CAP_PERFMON bypasses even paranoid=4. The IBS-Op lane is the exception: user-only sampling opens unprivileged at the default paranoid=2 via the kernel swfilt filter.

nodes.label: TSC clocksource gate (macOS clean room)
nodes.rationale: The Docker-OSX/KVM clean-room lane's hard gate: if host current_clocksource is not 'tsc', macOS guests (whose only timebase is the TSC) freeze under sustained load and no SMP/pin/-tsc-deadline combination survives — the only fix is a host reboot to re-measure TSC sync.

nodes.label: Zen 3 BRS non-functional; plan believes it works
nodes.rationale: Probe/capture open PERF_COUNT_HW_BRANCH_INSTRUCTIONS; on Fam19h kernel routes to amd_brs_hw_config which requires exactly event 0xc4 and sample_period>16, so BRS never opens. Misreported as AMD_NOHW. Blast radius bounded (cascades to DR/single-step, no wrong traces). Code fix hardware-blocked (no Zen3 box); the doc defects are not.
nodes.norm_label: zen 3 brs non-functional; plan believes it works

nodes.label: branchsnap synthetic edge inflates depth check by one
nodes.rationale: arr=[synthetic edge]+[use trimmed HW entries] passes n_dec=use+1 into a depth ceiling counting only HW slots, so a provably-complete use==15 window is flagged truncated. Fails safe but escalates to a real re-execution. Fix: gate on use, not n_dec.
nodes.norm_label: branchsnap synthetic edge inflates depth check by one

nodes.label: IBS_MAX_RECORD stale constant -> silent ring loss
nodes.rationale: 112-byte bound predates PERF_SAMPLE_CALLCHAIN; with callchain records reach ~1032-1184 bytes so the near-full-ring loss heuristic is ~10x short. PERF_RECORD_LOST does not cover the gap (a full ring yields lost==0). Window lane has no callchain gate.
nodes.norm_label: ibs_max_record stale constant -> silent ring loss

nodes.label: asmtest_amd_freeze_available dead code with live false docs
nodes.rationale: Definition with zero undefined references; gate deliberately removed (Zen5 disproved the theory) and replaced by an unconditional exit-presence check, but test_hwtrace prints false PRESENT/ABSENT strings and the plan text believes the opposite of the shipped code.
nodes.norm_label: asmtest_amd_freeze_available dead code with live false docs

nodes.label: AMD validation checklist stale and can pass vacuously
nodes.rationale: The only AMD gate that exists; one commit, identical timestamp to the fix commit. It gates on signals since measured false (ibs_probe misreports, make ibs-test vacuously green off-AMD) and inverts a regression signal into a known-false-green.
nodes.norm_label: amd validation checklist stale and can pass vacuously

nodes.label: IBS caps gate sufficient by unrecorded accident
nodes.rationale: Decoder never reads the record's caps word; length check cannot substitute (BrTarget vs OpData4 byte-identical length). Live path safe only because the kernel appends BrTarget before OpData4 and CPUID bit5 is gated - an append-order guarantee recorded nowhere in the tree. Exported pure decoder on foreign/VM records is the exposure.
nodes.norm_label: ibs caps gate sufficient by unrecorded accident

nodes.label: in-window SIGTRAP misclassified as BTF trap (app int3)
nodes.rationale: Drivers assume a SIGTRAP stop is their own #DB and never consult PTRACE_GETSIGINFO; an app int3 (JVM safepoint/.NET) is walked through and the block tail double-recorded with truncated=false. Fix: si_code TRAP_BRKPT split, in blockstep_reconstruct + region + window_block_walk. FIXED (T1/T2).
nodes.norm_label: in-window sigtrap misclassified as btf trap (app int3)

nodes.label: rep-prefixed string ops reconstructed once but retire N times
nodes.rationale: BTF records only control transfers so the walk advances by instruction length; rep stosq(RCX=8) walked once vs 8 per-instruction stops. Fix: detect rep prefix -> BS_AMBIGUOUS/truncated, never infer RCX statically. FIXED (T3).
nodes.norm_label: rep-prefixed string ops reconstructed once but retire n times

nodes.label: F1 emulator-replay tier structurally immune to the class
nodes.rationale: dataflow_blockstep executes each instruction through Unicorn with real register/flag state and reads back RIP, so a not-taken Jcc falls through and rep is seen N times; it never statically guesses the terminator. Cost: needs an emulator that can execute the instruction (the AVX gate).
nodes.norm_label: f1 emulator-replay tier structurally immune to the class

nodes.label: scoped call-out step-over fabricates the edge F6 fixed
nodes.rationale: A caller-saved register clobbered by a stepped-over helper hands a post-gap read to the stale in-region writer: the VALUE stays faithful, only the EDGE lies, so no value oracle or byte-identical comparison can catch it. Fix (landed): snapshot the risk set at gap entry, diff at exit, emit one GAP step via dfp_emit_gap.
nodes.norm_label: scoped call-out step-over fabricates the edge f6 fixed

nodes.label: covered(t,0) is vacuous (amd_replay appends block 0)
nodes.rationale: amd_backend appends block 0 unconditionally so covered(t,0) is always true; the branchsnap test's entry evidence is carried entirely by ni>0 beside it. Fixed at the assertion site to path-specific covered(want)&&!covered(other), live-verified on Zen5 LbrExtV2.

nodes.label: blockstep suite re-declares struct with no layout guard
nodes.rationale: Tier ships no header (keeps producer off ABI) so the suite re-declares asmtest_blockstep_info_t with 0 sizeof/offsetof guards; a field skew that lands in tail padding passes a size-only guard (F6 hit this). Fix pins size AND final-field offset. Landed.
nodes.norm_label: blockstep suite re-declares struct with no layout guard

nodes.label: rdtsc/cpuid are a PRIMITIVE gap, not a decode gap
nodes.rationale: PTRACE_SINGLEBLOCK (BTF) traps only control transfers; rdtsc/rdtscp/rdrand/rdseed/cpuid are not control transfers so BTF gives no boundary - no decoding helps. Needs a hardware execution breakpoint (DR0-3), landed as T5+T6. sysenter still gated.
nodes.norm_label: rdtsc/cpuid are a primitive gap, not a decode gap

nodes.label: an assertion's discriminating power must be demonstrated, not assumed
nodes.rationale: A value oracle cannot see a fabricated edge; covered(t,0) cannot fail; a sizeof guard cannot see a field that fits in padding - each looks like coverage and provides none.
nodes.norm_label: an assertion's discriminating power must be demonstrated, not assumed

nodes.label: SDE future/absent-ISA test lane - the one to build
nodes.rationale: Pin is SDE's substrate; SDE emulates APX/AVX10.2/AMX/AVX-512 at instrumentation time. A true DR impossibility (DR runs on real silicon) and beyond Unicorn (QEMU 5.0.1 predates AVX TCG). Converts a hardware self-skip into an installable, CI-runnable lane. Shipped.

nodes.rationale: Pin decodes with XED (updated in lockstep with silicon); DR's own decoder lags (APX #6226 open) so a routine using r16-r31 cannot pass DR's code cache today. Currency-bounded gap, not a permanent architectural one.

nodes.label: Pin probe mode - instrumentation with no code cache
nodes.rationale: Probe mode trampolines function boundaries and runs original code natively; DR has no supported equivalent. Weakest exclusivity (approximable via hand-rolled/Frida hooks) - a robustness win for arg/return capture, not a hard capability.
nodes.norm_label: pin probe mode - instrumentation with no code cache

nodes.label: libdft64 differential taint oracle for the DR client
nodes.rationale: libdft64 is the canonical peer-reviewed byte-level taint engine on Pin; diffed byte-for-byte against the home-grown DR client it is the strongest cross-validation. Oracle-hardening, not new reach. Shipped.

nodes.label: AArch64 ptrace-emulation options on an x86 host

nodes.label: qemu-user is a dead end for ptrace (by design)
nodes.rationale: ISA-only emulation (qemu-user/binfmt/TCG, Docker buildx, Lima Fast mode) cannot back PTRACE_SINGLESTEP - passing guest ptrace to the host kernel would expose QEMU's own x86 state; do_ptrace is an ENOSYS stub. This is what probe_singlestep detects and self-skips.
nodes.norm_label: qemu-user is a dead end for ptrace (by design)

nodes.label: qemu-system-aarch64 (full-system TCG) works, slow
nodes.rationale: Full-system TCG implements the ARMv8 software-step state machine (since 2014) so a real guest kernel drives PTRACE_SINGLESTEP; software single-step only (HW breakpoint later/weaker), documented correctness bugs, pure-TCG slow. Marginal vs the hosted arm64 runners.

nodes.label: native arm64 silicon - the low-friction route the tree uses
nodes.rationale: A real arm64 kernel+CPU is where ptrace/single-step just work; ubuntu-24.04-arm runners (free public, $0.005/min private) already cover hwtrace-arm64. Guarded by an anti-vacuity assert so a qemu-style self-skip is a red build.
nodes.norm_label: native arm64 silicon - the low-friction route the tree uses

nodes.label: CoreSight ETM is real-silicon-only (not modelled by virt)
nodes.rationale: QEMU virt models no trace macrocell, so ETM capture/decode needs real arm64 silicon with CoreSight - full-system qemu does not rescue it (absence-of-evidence, medium confidence).

nodes.label: five capture approaches (LD_PRELOAD/DBI/ptrace/uprobes-eBPF/PLT-GOT)
nodes.rationale: LD_PRELOAD = fastest rich semantic traces for a small function set; ptrace = straightest live-attach mapping at high cost; uprobes/eBPF = good production balance (limited derefs); DBI (DynamoRIO from launch) = full-scale long-running. Never trust pointer validity; cap reads.

nodes.rationale: Per step, {tagged_location, size, value, is_write} where location carries its space (reg-id / absolute-addr / routine-offset) - the address-space normalization contract, keyed off capture mode. Needs the .access field for direction and regs_read/write+eflags for implicit operands.

nodes.label: L1 def-use graph (last-writer linker)
nodes.rationale: A last-writer map (reg->step, mem-byte->step) emitting producer->consumer edges. Register def-use is a straight offline pass; MEMORY def-use is not tier-neutral - keys on raw addresses that change meaning across a GC compaction.

nodes.rationale: on_code fires before the instruction; load-value capture needs UC_HOOK_MEM_READ_AFTER, mem hooks must be armed unconditionally. Re-executes extracted bytes in a virtual guest - faithful only for a self-contained (OS-interaction-free) deterministic region; the value engine bolted onto a cheap live capture (snapshot-seeded or path replay).

nodes.label: out-of-process ptrace stepper - the out-of-band live-managed tier
nodes.rationale: Reads the tracee's real state so values are real, and is out-of-band so it doesn't fight the runtime's signal/JIT/code-cache. Full GETREGS is already there; add GETFPREGS/NT_X86_XSTATE, per-operand effective-address compute + process_vm_readv (+ fs_base/gs_base for .NET TLS). Cost ~10^3-10^5x; bound by a using scope.

nodes.label: hardware tier cannot alone (PTWRITE/PEBS-IBS/PT+replay)
nodes.rationale: Silicon emits control-flow, no operand-value channel. Escape hatches: PTWRITE (needs instrumentation, Alder-Lake+), PEBS/IBS statistical data-ADDRESS sampling (partial, address not value), or PT control-flow + emulator replay + input capture (PANDA taint2 / TTD exemplars; rr does NOT belong here). CoreSight has no PTWRITE equivalent.

nodes.label: memory def-use gated on GC-move canonicalization
nodes.rationale: Under a moving GC a raw address changes meaning across compaction, so coherent memory flow needs (object,field) canonicalization from GC-move events; EventPipe GCBulkMovedObjectRanges (OldRangeBase/NewRangeBase/RangeLength, cross-platform ETW twin) carries it, MethodLoadVerbose (id 143) for method identity.
nodes.norm_label: memory def-use gated on gc-move canonicalization

nodes.label: native external attach GO (drrun -attach on pinned DR)
nodes.rationale: drrun -attach <pid> -c <client> takes a running native process over, the drmgr bb event fires over live code (1.6B instrumented insns), the victim survives and exits native. Gotchas: -attach must precede -c; CAP_SYS_PTRACE is required and sufficient (bypasses yama). Unblocks attach-tier Increments 3-5; managed stays research-gated.
nodes.norm_label: native external attach go (drrun -attach on pinned dr)

nodes.label: prebuilt drmgr/drreg/drx load under the private loader (option c wins)
nodes.rationale: The long-documented 'extensions won't load on modern glibc' blocker does NOT reproduce at glibc 2.39 + pinned DR 11.91.20630; the extensions load and instrument (130588 insns). drx_buf is not a separate extension (it is in drx). Choose version-pin; the re-platform is unblocked with no loader workaround.
nodes.norm_label: prebuilt drmgr/drreg/drx load under the private loader (option c wins)

nodes.label: umbra is LGPL-2.1 (license split contradicts the plan)
nodes.rationale: drmgr/drreg/drx are BSD (DR core) but umbra ships under Dr. Memory Framework as LGPL-2.1 - the same obligation as drwrap the tier refuses. Loadability is not the umbra problem, licensing is. Default: hand-roll a BSD direct-mapped shadow instead of umbra.
nodes.norm_label: umbra is lgpl-2.1 (license split contradicts the plan)

nodes.label: managed external attach NO-GO (stack-smashing SIGSEGV at takeover)
nodes.rationale: drrun -attach delivers and starts the client (dr_client_main runs) but the takeover trips glibc stack-smashing and the process dies SIGSEGV rc139 - DR seizing the .NET runtime's threads (GC/JIT/finalizer) at arbitrary state. It is the SEIZE not instrumentation (noinstr crashes identically); no DR option/version helps. Managed stays on launch-under-DR / ptrace.
nodes.norm_label: managed external attach no-go (stack-smashing sigsegv at takeover)

nodes.label: safepoint spike also NO-GO (native runtime threads unparkable)
nodes.rationale: SuspendRuntime parks all MANAGED threads at GC-safe points (hr=0), then DR-attaches the parked process - and the seize still SIGSEGVs identically. Decisive: the fatal takeover is of the NATIVE runtime threads (GC/JIT/finalizer/diagnostics-IPC) a managed-only suspend cannot park. Both options exhausted.
nodes.norm_label: safepoint spike also no-go (native runtime threads unparkable)

nodes.label: profiler attach GO - MovedReferences2 delivers post-attach
nodes.rationale: A CLR profiler attaches to an already-running dotnet with no CORECLR_* env, over the diagnostics port, and receives MovedReferences2 {old,new,len} triples (160,032 relocating of 160,064 across 320 post-attach GCs, SetEventMask S_OK). F4's GC-move feed is NOT limited to launched targets. Distinct from DR attach: this is a cooperative path the runtime drives at its own fences.
nodes.norm_label: profiler attach go - movedreferences2 delivers post-attach

nodes.label: InitializeForAttach path (ICorProfilerCallback3, not Initialize)
nodes.rationale: An attaching profiler gets InitializeForAttach + ProfilerAttachComplete (never Initialize); QI for ICorProfilerCallback3 is load-bearing and must reject Callback5+. cbClientData can hand config (e.g. an shm channel name) at attach time.

nodes.label: freeze assumption is FALSE -> stamp with profiler-sampled S0
nodes.rationale: A ptrace-single-stepped managed thread retires ~420 instructions across every GC fence (47/47), not zero - the thread IS futex-blocked but single-stepping un-blocks it (each stop interrupts, each step restarts the wait loop; zero samples in the JIT heap). Drain-time stamping is unsound; stamp asmtest_gcmove_t.step with S0 captured inside GarbageCollectionStarted.
nodes.norm_label: freeze assumption is false -> stamp with profiler-sampled s0

nodes.label: GC stall/livelock hazard while single-stepping a managed thread
nodes.rationale: A GC fence often cannot complete at all while a managed thread is stepped: RuntimeSuspendStarted fires, the runtime hammers the stepped thread with SIGRTMIN activation injections and never reaches RuntimeSuspendFinished, hanging the whole process (~19.8s) until detach. An availability hazard for the live-attach managed tier - step in short bursts under the GC interval.
nodes.norm_label: gc stall/livelock hazard while single-stepping a managed thread

nodes.label: GCBulkNode addresses are POST-move (GO)
nodes.rationale: All 15001 of the dump GC's own relocating ranges have a node at NewRangeBase and zero at OldRangeBase (post_witness=15001 pre_witness=0) - node.Address is the final resting place, so the dump GC's own move ranges BELONG in the trace->snapshot translation set (T5 must include, not filter, the last post-capture gc_seq). MovedReferences2 fires pre-relocation while the GCBulkNode walk runs post-relocation - consistent, one old->new map.

nodes.label: ICorProfilerCallback4::MovedReferences2 (recommended, in-process)
nodes.rationale: A native in-process CLR profiler delivers exact per-range {old,new,len} as three parallel arrays - the payload IS the triple, no schema parsing. Fires only on real (compacting) moves, at a fully-suspended-EE fence, co-located so it calls at_gc_remap directly and synchronously. Tradeoff: COR_PRF_MONITOR_GC disables background GC. Probe confirmed it coexists with DynamoRIO (GO).

nodes.label: out-of-process EventPipe + TraceEvent (fallback)
nodes.rationale: GCBulkMovedObjectRangesTraceData.Values[] exposes OldRangeBase/NewRangeBase/RangeLength under the GCHeapSurvivalAndMovement keyword (0x400000). The fallback, not the pick: cross-process, higher latency, and EventPipe drops/truncates under load -> silent tag corruption for a shadow remap. The in-proc EventListener (Candidate 3) only hands back a scalar count - a dead end.

nodes.norm_label: can native trace points be mapped to il / bytecode

nodes.label: the deciding split - JIT'd recoverable, interpreted not
nodes.rationale: For JIT'd code the native PC IS the managed machine code and the runtime emits a native->IL/bci table you can join (buildable). For interpreted code the PC sits in the shared eval loop and the live bytecode index lives in VM register/frame state a control-flow-only trace cannot observe - not recoverable from the offset stream, needs a state probe. Same wall CPython hits.
nodes.norm_label: the deciding split - jit'd recoverable, interpreted not

nodes.label: stop discarding JIT_CODE_DEBUG_INFO - the cheapest first step
nodes.rationale: asmtest_jitdump_find parsed only JIT_CODE_LOAD, skipping the JIT_CODE_DEBUG_INFO (addr,line,file) records it already receives from libperf-jvmti / V8 --perf-prof; consuming them yields address->source-line across JVM and V8 with no new agent. Now parsed and bridged into the line map (T1).
nodes.norm_label: stop discarding jit_code_debug_info - the cheapest first step

nodes.label: hardware trace is the way around JITs (out-of-band)
nodes.rationale: Stop instrumenting and start observing: Intel PT / CoreSight ETM record control flow out-of-band with no code cache, no hijacked SIGSEGV, no W^X thrash - so they don't collide with a runtime's JIT/GC/signal machinery the way in-process DBI does. ~2-20% overhead, 0 detached, no cooperation.
nodes.norm_label: hardware trace is the way around jits (out-of-band)

nodes.label: the one hard problem is temporal (userspace TEXT_POKE)
nodes.rationale: PT/ETM emit no instruction bytes; the decoder needs the code image live at each trace position, but code at a JIT address changes/frees/reuses over time and libipt has no temporal model. A single late snapshot returns wrong bytes; the answer is a timestamped code-image timeline reproducing kernel PERF_RECORD_TEXT_POKE semantics in userspace.
nodes.norm_label: the one hard problem is temporal (userspace text_poke)

nodes.label: time-aware code-image recorder (asmtest_codeimage)
nodes.rationale: A userspace PERF_RECORD_TEXT_POKE building a timestamped code-image timeline cross-process via soft-dirty + PAGEMAP_SCAN, bytes via process_vm_readv, with an optional eBPF emission detector on mprotect/mmap/memfd_create. Supports pid==0 (self). Shipped; feeds the ptrace stepper and the libipt PT decoder.

nodes.label: L3 DESCEND_ALL is hazardous on a live runtime (can deadlock)
nodes.rationale: The single-tid stepper single-steps one thread ~1000x slower while siblings run free; if descended code holds a lock a sibling needs (GC alloc slow-path, JIT-compile helper, ld.so resolver, malloc arena) the sibling stalls and a watchdog cannot break it. GC/re-JIT can move code from under the stepper. L3's denylist/budget/watchdog is damage limitation, not a guarantee - use on safe-by-construction targets.
nodes.norm_label: l3 descend_all is hazardous on a live runtime (can deadlock)

nodes.label: four ranked attach-at-runtime approaches
nodes.rationale: 1 PT + runtime-enabled jitdump (lowest, production; often no launch flag - .NET EnablePerfMap over the diag port, JVM jcmd JVMTI.agent_load); 2 PT + eBPF/uffd time-aware recorder (buildable core); 3 hypervisor host-PT + EPT execute-trap (research-grade); 4 deterministic record/replay (TTD/rr, solves bytes by re-running).

nodes.label: FFI-shaped C-ABI surface - yes to run/test/call, one or two calls
nodes.rationale: The framework's value-add is a flat C-ABI (pointers, long arrays, fixed-layout structs) so anything with a C FFI can consume it. Execute/validate already decompose into two entry points; regs_t is an immutable snapshot in host memory (not a live view) so arbitrary host code between the calls is safe by construction. The one irreducible native artifact is the compiled capture trampoline.
nodes.norm_label: ffi-shaped c-abi surface - yes to run/test/call, one or two calls

nodes.label: crash safety is the one real design decision (route via emulator)
nodes.rationale: A thin direct-FFI call bypasses the runner's fork isolation, so a faulting routine takes down the host. Routing execution through the emulator turns faults into return values (emu_result_t faulted/fault_addr) - the strongest cross-language story; else fork/subprocess the call or accept a loud native crash.
nodes.norm_label: crash safety is the one real design decision (route via emulator)

nodes.label: effort tracks GC behaviour (pin buffers; emulator memory is disjoint)
nodes.rationale: Moving GC (Go/JVM/.NET/JS) can relocate a buffer mid-call so it must be pinned; non-moving/no-GC (Python/Rust/Zig) is friction-free. The emulator path neutralises it (guest memory is disjoint - stage bytes in, copy out). Python first (lowest friction proves the substrate), Rust second (no-GC/auto-bindgen); Go highest friction, prefer the emulator path.
nodes.norm_label: effort tracks gc behaviour (pin buffers; emulator memory is disjoint)

nodes.label: Non-intrusive in-process managed tracing - the scoped using model
nodes.norm_label: non-intrusive in-process managed tracing - the scoped using model

nodes.label: a using-block is an enable/disable window; non-intrusive = HW trace
nodes.rationale: A using block maps exactly onto asmtest_hwtrace begin/end (self, per-thread, self-attached). Non-intrusive AND in-process narrows to PT/LBR/CoreSight; the empty ctor 'handles everything' because out-of-band capture is capture-everything-then-filter-at-decode (no method address, no knowledge). Three host preconditions (privilege, Intel bare metal, temporal bytes - easier in-process via the self code-image recorder) can only be detected and self-skipped, not coded away.
nodes.norm_label: a using-block is an enable/disable window; non-intrusive = hw trace

nodes.label: five non-intrusiveness axes (only HW trace passes all)
nodes.rationale: No code modification; no signal/exception hijacking; no thread perturbation; no memory-protection interference; bounded timing overhead. Single-step fails axes 2/3/5 on a managed runtime; DR fails the deployment axis; only out-of-band hardware trace passes all five.
nodes.norm_label: five non-intrusiveness axes (only hw trace passes all)

nodes.label: the scope is a THREAD scope, not a logical-operation scope
nodes.rationale: The perf event follows the calling thread (pid==0,cpu==-1), so await/Task.Run/thread-pool continuations are not captured and an await can resume Dispose() on a different thread. The deep qualification (vs the buildable Q2/Q3/Q4 engineering gaps): follow the logical operation via an AsyncLocal value-changed hook and stitch per-thread slices by ScopeId. Flag on a thread-id mismatch, same never-emit-partial posture as truncated.
nodes.norm_label: the scope is a thread scope, not a logical-operation scope

nodes.label: .NET 8+ closes the leaks (runtime events supply addresses)
nodes.rationale: MethodLoadVerbose_V2 (JITKeyword) carries MethodStartAddress/Size/name/ReJITID, consumable in-process by a plain EventListener - no file, IPC, privilege or launch flag. This retires the broken PrepareMethod+GetFunctionPointer path (leak 2); EnablePerfMap(sendExisting=true) / EventPipe rundown cover pre-arm methods (leak 3); leak 1 contracts to 'you must name the method' plus an inlining caveat (detect via JITTracingKeyword, or undo via RequestReJITWithInliners).
nodes.norm_label: .net 8+ closes the leaks (runtime events supply addresses)

nodes.label: Trace parity matrix (analysis)
nodes.rationale: Consolidated cross-checked reference for which trace backends work on which hardware/OS/microarchitecture/language; one universal emulator floor plus a fragmented set of native tiers all filling the same asmtest_trace_t shape, so a test swaps backends without changing coverage reads.

nodes.label: Tracing backend decision matrix (analysis)
nodes.rationale: Decision aid choosing a backend by three axes resolved in order: arch x OS decides what exists, language class decides what is SAFE (managed single-step is fatal), capture goal decides fast-vs-complete. Also breaks out host provisioning (generic vs docker-lane vs full-permission).

nodes.label: Emulator (Unicorn) trace tier
nodes.rationale: Universal floor for every OS/arch/language the native tiers cannot reach; a virtual guest not the real CPU. The only tier offering cross-ISA guests (x86-64/Win64/AArch64/RISC-V/ARM32), isolated guest memory and faults-as-data. Coverage-equivalent to native only for pure-compute routines.

nodes.label: DynamoRIO DBI trace tier
nodes.rationale: Only vendor- and microarchitecture-independent native backend shipping today (Linux x86-64, every Intel + every Zen); native-speed code cache, exact and unbounded, BSD core (deliberately no drwrap LGPL). Cannot take over managed JIT/GC threads (Node/.NET self-skip).

nodes.label: Intel PT hardware trace
nodes.rationale: Continuous branch-trace AUX ring decoded by libipt; near-zero overhead, exact and unbounded; bare-metal Intel Linux only. Out-of-band, so the clean recommended tier for managed runtimes on Intel (no thread takeover, no signal collision).

nodes.label: AMD LBR branch-record tier
nodes.rationale: 16-deep branch stack (Tier-A exact within one window; Tier-B stitches sample_period=1 windows past 16, bounded by ring + PMI throttling). Zen 4/5 LbrExtV2 is the live-capture floor (live-verified on a Zen 5 Ryzen 9 9950X); Zen 3 BRS exists in silicon but this tree cannot open it; Zen 2 has no branch facility.

nodes.label: ARM CoreSight (ETM/ETE) trace
nodes.rationale: Exact real-CPU trace on aarch64 with a CoreSight-capable board, decoded by OpenCSD; decoder coarser and normalized to match. Reconstruction core is host-validated but live decode awaits a board (self-skips).

nodes.label: In-process single-step (EFLAGS.TF) tier
nodes.rationale: EFLAGS.TF -> #DB/SIGTRAP records every executed RIP; exact, unbounded, unprivileged and CI-safe, x86-only (~2.3us/insn). Shipped on Linux x86-64, macOS-Intel, and Windows via VEH. FATAL on a managed-runtime thread that blocks SIGTRAP (exit 133).

nodes.label: Out-of-process ptrace single-step tier (W2)
nodes.rationale: A tracer parent PTRACE_SINGLESTEPs a forked/attached tracee and reconstructs the same offsets out of band -- the managed-runtime path, the only backend whose observer lives in a different process from the traced code. Linux x86-64 shipped; AArch64 code-complete but its live stream is HW-pending (qemu-user cannot emulate ptrace).

nodes.label: asmtest_trace_t shared trace shape
nodes.rationale: The canonical trace model every backend fills: ordered instruction offsets, distinct basic-block offsets, dynamic totals, and a truncation bit, all normalized to a single offset basis. This data-shape parity is what lets one backend stand in for another without rewriting assertions.

nodes.label: Descending-fidelity fallback cascade
nodes.rationale: Two primitives make it tractable: a static available()/skip_reason probe (init-time) and the dynamic truncated bit (runtime). native->native falls are transparent; a native->emulator fall crosses a semantic fidelity line and must be an explicit opt-in (NATIVE_ONLY forbids the silent crossing).

nodes.label: asmtest_trace_call_auto / trace_resolve orchestrator
nodes.rationale: Cross-tier front-end that walks the full descending-fidelity cascade (Intel PT -> AMD LBR -> DynamoRIO -> single-step -> CoreSight -> emulator) returning tier/backend/fidelity descriptors; call_auto additionally owns the invocation so it can re-run and escalate on truncated. DynamoRIO ranks above single-step (native-speed cache vs per-insn kernel round-trip).

nodes.label: AMD LBR BPF boundary snapshot (#3)
nodes.rationale: bpf_get_branch_snapshot freezes at a hardware #DB exit breakpoint in kernel context (zero userspace glue) -- the clean deterministic boundary capture; exact for a tiny routine (<=16 branches), near-zero overhead. Needs CAP_BPF + Zen 4/5 + kernel >=6.10 + a libbpf build.

nodes.label: AMD LBR MSR-direct snapshot
nodes.rationale: Reads the LbrExtV2 branch-record MSRs directly around a region for an exact Tier-A snapshot with zero PMU interrupts; contamination-limited because the freeze syscall's glue branches eat the 16-entry window. Higher-privilege niche (CAP_SYS_ADMIN + msr module) vs the BPF snapshot's cleaner boundary.

nodes.label: AMD LBR WindowHot statistical survey
nodes.rationale: A sampled hot-method histogram, not an exact path (IsStatistical); near-native (a few PMIs), crash-proof over managed code, and because the block runs at native speed it gives the richest managed attribution. Never feeds the exact insns[]/blocks[] parity cascade.

nodes.label: AMD IBS-Op statistical survey source
nodes.rationale: A second survey source under the branch-stack survey tier, ordered strictly after it; on Zen 2 (no branch facility) it flattens each sampled edge target into the same endpoint histogram. Survey-only, never the exact insns[]/blocks[] fidelity cascade; user-only IBS opens unprivileged at paranoid=2 via the kernel swfilt bit.

nodes.label: BTF block-step (PTRACE_SINGLEBLOCK)
nodes.rationale: Exact, complete, rootless, ~1 trap per taken branch -- the key ceiling-free middle rung the static resolve cascade lacks (block-step is a ptrace entry, not a resolve backend). Linux x86-64 only; no aarch64 form (falls to per-insn); self-skips masked-DEBUGCTL.BTF VMs.

nodes.label: Win64 VEH single-step
nodes.rationale: AddVectoredExceptionHandler stepper covering x86-64 Windows (~6x), the Windows analog of the in-process single-step backend; exact and complete.

nodes.label: AMD MSR-direct LBR snapshot plan
nodes.rationale: Reads the LbrExtV2 MSRs directly (enable/reset/run/freeze/read 16 FROM/TO) via /dev/cpu/N/msr, decoded by the shared asmtest_amd_decode -- a zero-interrupt, libbpf-free Tier-A tier for a CAP_SYS_ADMIN self-hosted runner. LANDED and empirically validated on Zen 5 (a 4-trip loop captures complete, not truncated); contamination-limited by the freeze-syscall glue.

nodes.label: AMD review follow-ups (P1-P9)
nodes.rationale: Actions the confirmed findings of the 2026-07-17 AMD hardware review (four of nine refuted). P1-P8 landed (validation-checklist repair, branchsnap depth-check on use, IBS_MAX_RECORD callchain sizing, Zen 3 BRS docs truth, freeze-probe retirement, install asmtest_ibs.h, IBS caps append-order, sample_period exercise); P9 self-hosted Zen runner is the sole open, infra-gated item. Organising fact: the AMD code is ahead of the process that validates it.

nodes.label: AMD tracing 10-item follow-up (Phases 1-10)
nodes.rationale: Ten concrete improvements to the AMD branch-record tier, all LANDED: struct_size ABI guard, overflow-safe nr clamp, EPERM/status/paranoid surface, env-gated debug logging, multi-exit deterministic BPF boundary snapshot (default-on for 1..4 exits), cascade-comment fix, IBS-Op survey fallback (superseded by the zen2-ibs plan), non-blocking snapshot drain, cached cpuinfo-flag probe, and the AMD LBR window-reach tuning guide. House rule: no untested hardware code.

nodes.label: .NET AsmTrace whole-window family (E1-E7)
nodes.rationale: Keeps the .NET whole-window forms coherent under different fidelity/crash-safety/overhead trades: WindowHybrid (survey->exact on the hot slice), AsmMethod.Weight, sibling-thread live JIT publish, AutoFDO weighting, snapshot-tiling/IBS producers into WindowHot, and an AMD-LBR region example. E1-E7 all landed; E4 inline OOP built but strictly worse than the AsmTrace.Window factory.

nodes.label: AsmTrace inline-using conformance (R1-R4)
nodes.rationale: Makes the inline `using (new AsmTrace(...))` scope shape work for every trace form in addition to the delegate factories. START/STOP backends (single-step TF, AMD LBR perf, Intel PT AUX) are trivial; the out-of-process reverse-attach stepper is a hard COORDINATION case needing an async begin/end stop-flag split. PT inline is silicon-validated; OOP inline is strictly worse than the factory.

nodes.label: Auto-escalating cross-tier trace plan
nodes.rationale: A call-owning entry point (asmtest_trace_call_auto) that traces a routine under the fastest exact tier and automatically escalates to a ceiling-free tier on truncated -- closing the arm->detect->re-resolve->re-run loop that was only a documented idiom. Ladder: fast HWTRACE backend -> BTF block-step (the rung the static cascade lacks) -> per-insn single-step; DynamoRIO/emulator excluded (no call-owning entry / fidelity crossing). Requires re-runnable/deterministic code.

nodes.label: Binding coverage parity plan
nodes.rationale: Closes gaps where the C core exposed emulator/assembler capability no language binding could reach (cross-arch guests arm64/riscv/arm, FP/vector/6-arg/Win64 emu calls, execution-trace handle, asm tier corpus anchor). Cross-arch guests run raw machine-code bytes so they emulate on any host; result structs share a leading layout reusing the emu_result accessors. Complete across all ten bindings.

nodes.label: Bundle native-trace tiers into packages
nodes.rationale: Ship DynamoRIO (drapp+drclient+libdynamorio, linux-x86_64 slot) and hardware-trace (libasmtest_hwtrace, every Linux slot) inside the six prebuilt-payload packages so a fresh install runs NativeTrace/HwTrace with no manual make and no DYNAMORIO_HOME. hwtrace is nearly free (decoder-free build reuses vendored Capstone); DynamoRIO is heavy (~doubles the Linux slot); available() semantics unchanged.

nodes.label: Call-descent for the ptrace tracer (levels 0-3)
nodes.rationale: Adds optional levels of descent into the call-outs the out-of-process ptrace stepper currently steps over: OFF / RECORD_EDGES / DESCEND_KNOWN / DESCEND_ALL. A new opaque asmtest_descent_t handle keeps asmtest_trace_t byte-frozen; correctness rests on a return-address shadow stack with an exact pop predicate + SP-sweep. L3 is default-off (the live-runtime cross-thread lock-inversion deadlock vector is not fully mitigable).

nodes.label: Cross-system performance & feature benchmarking
nodes.rationale: One runner emits a per-system report merging a performance benchmark (real cycles + deterministic emulated insn/block counts) and a feature benchmark (a live capability sweep of every trace tier/backend). Deterministic emu counts persist as gated golden files; real cycles as per-box history. Instantiates the trace-parity matrices live per system; never subtract across units; absent capability is data.

nodes.label: Data-flow tracing (L0/L1/L2) plan
nodes.rationale: Adds a shared L0 value-trace sink (asmtest_valtrace_t) plus tier-neutral L1 def-use and L2 taint/slicing passes built once over L0, mirroring the asmtest_trace_t discipline. Producers: emulator (CI oracle), scoped ptrace stepper (real live out-of-band values), DynamoRIO (production in-band taint over managed code, ~11x bare). The .NET interpretability layer (PC->method, GC-move canonicalization) makes managed taint meaningful.

nodes.rationale: One binding fix (AmdSnapshot P/Invoke) + 13 new .NET examples exercising bound-but-undemoed AsmTrace/HwTrace/Ptrace APIs and real workflows (regression diff, perf triage, crash-proof showdown, tier ladder, AMD period sweep/snapshot). Deferred five candidates that would only ever self-skip, duplicate, or flake -- the truthful call.

nodes.rationale: Separates what can be reported cheaply from AsmTrace.Addresses (tiers, hotspots, flat-profile, amplification, runtime-gaps, footprint, runtimebuckets) from new example projects. The genuine currency is instruction counts, not time (~1M-insn amplification makes any time number meaningless). Out-of-process ptrace/descent examples for what in-process single-step structurally cannot do (managed attach, exact call tree).

nodes.label: .NET managed multi-threaded live-PT concurrency fix
nodes.rationale: The one blocker after Intel PT was validated on silicon: the .NET managed multi-threaded live-PT suite raced non-deterministically. Root cause pinned by eu-stack was an unsynchronized asmtest_codeimage use-after-free (the JIT thread realloc'ing region/version arrays a per-tid PT hop decode was walking). Fixed with a codeimage mutex + ordered ambient-hop lifetime; crash 7/7 -> 0/8; libipt-dev re-added to the dotnet image.

nodes.label: dotnet-parity roadmap (nine bindings vs .NET)
nodes.rationale: Retires the ALL-exemptions the symbol-name parity gate consumes -- the .NET-lead surface. Splits generic C primitives (any binding can wrap) from managed-JIT capabilities (live JIT-output tracing + async-hop stitching) which exist only in Node/Java. Six non-managed bindings reach primitive-surface parity only; a green gate is not feature parity.

nodes.label: Dependency-free in-process jitdump rundown
nodes.rationale: Makes the whole-window managed-method breakdown name warm + ReadyToRun (R2R) BCL methods, not only cold methods JIT'd inside the scope, without a NuGet dependency. Hand-rolls one diagnostics-IPC EnablePerfMap(JitDump) message over the runtime's Unix socket and reads the binary jitdump (R2R names go only there, never the text perf-map). Opt-in via AsmTrace(withRundown), self-skips cleanly.

nodes.label: DynamoRIO external-attach tier
nodes.rationale: The third DR integration model: attach the in-band taint client to an already-running native process (dr_inject_process_attach / drrun -attach), instrument a scoped region, drain over shm, and detach -- ~10-50x while armed, ~0 detached. External attach is GO for native (validated: 1.6B insns, victim survives, K=3 re-attach reliable) but NO-GO for managed (a DR seize trips stack-smashing SIGSEGV). Reuses the taint client/shm/validator verbatim.

nodes.label: DynamoRIO managed attach via GC safepoints
nodes.rationale: The Option-2 follow-on to the attach tier's Increment-6 NO-GO: park every managed thread at a GC-safe point (profiler SuspendRuntime) before the DR seize, then take over, then resume. SPIKE EXECUTED -- Increment 1 GO (suspension works under DR), Increment 2 NO-GO (a fully parked runtime still crashes identically). Decisive: the fatal takeover is the native runtime threads a managed suspend cannot park. Managed stays launch-under-DR / ptrace-attach.

nodes.label: .NET managed-code capability (§D0: MethodLoadVerbose/JitMethodMap, AsmStitchedTrace)
nodes.rationale: §D0 LANDED. JitMethodMap in-proc MethodLoadVerbose_V2 EventListener resolves (address,size,version); DiagnosticsIpc EnablePerfMap(JitDump) pre-arm rundown; AsmTrace.Method named-method step-over; AsyncLocal<ScopeId> value-changed hook (AsmStitchedTrace) is the flagship async-hop producer feeding the merge core.

nodes.label: Node scope construct + AsyncStitchedTrace (§D1)
nodes.rationale: §D1 LANDED incl. using/Symbol.dispose sugar (its syntax half self-skips below Node 24). AsyncStitchedTrace over AsyncLocalStorage/async_hooks orders same-thread async only; genuine cross-thread (worker_threads/libuv-pool) escapes and is a disclosed gap. An adversarial review caught a per-scope owned-trace use-after-free on a shared call-site region name (fixed via slot reclaim + tombstone).

nodes.label: JVM scope construct + propagating executor decorator (§D2)
nodes.rationale: §D2 LANDED. try-with-resources AsmTrace; address resolution reuses the libperf-jvmti.so jitdump agent read in-process via asmtest_jitdump_find (must discover the randomized $HOME/.debug/jit dir). Shipped async-hop producer is the propagating executor decorator carrying ScopeId across a hop into the merge.
nodes.norm_label: jvm scope construct + propagating executor decorator (§d2)

nodes.label: JVMTI zero-touch hop hook — DECIDED NO-GO (2026-07-17)
nodes.rationale: NO-GO on evidence, not cost. JVMTI has no value-changed event; HotSpot VirtualThreadMount/Unmount extension events fire only where a vthread IS the Thread object (id already follows unaided) and never for the platform-thread submit() the decorator serves — complementary populations, so the agent would work and buy nothing. Measured on JDK 25: 60 mount/60 unmount for vthreads, 0 for ExecutorService.submit; 8/8 vthreads kept their ThreadLocal across carrier migration. The one route that sees the submit (CLASS_FILE_LOAD_HOOK bytecode instrumentation) is declined on cost/benefit.
nodes.norm_label: jvmti zero-touch hop hook — decided no-go (2026-07-17)

nodes.label: Concealed out-of-process ptrace stealth stepper (§D3, asmtest_hwtrace_stealth_trace)
nodes.rationale: §D3 LANDED. Reverse-attaches to the caller (PR_SET_PTRACER_ANY + PTRACE_SEIZE), run_to's region entry, single-steps out of band. Standalone asmtest-stealth-helper binary discovered via dladdr sibling, scratch handed over a memfd. State-safe (touches no signals/bytes/protections), timing-intrusive (~1000x). Live-JIT cross-process address channel (asmtest_addr_channel.h header-only SPSC ring) + windowed capture landed, incl. .NET composition (E3).

nodes.label: Async-hop stitching merge core (§D4, asmtest_hwtrace_stitch + slice/bound ABI)
nodes.rationale: §D4: the Q1 model change — the scope stops being a thread window and becomes a stitched trace of one logical operation. Shared pure ordered merge over per-thread PT slices already decoded against their window-live code-image version (temporal-bytes rule), so close is a pure concatenation; host-testable from synthetic pre-decoded slices (test_stitch_slices). Two of three live producers ship (.NET/Node); JVM decided NO-GO.

nodes.label: Region-free whole-window arm surface (§Z0, asmtest_hwtrace_begin_window)
nodes.rationale: §Z0 LANDED across all 10 bindings. begin_window/_end_window/_render_window legitimately permit a NULL/zero-len range: bypasses find_region, never calls register_region, carries arm_tid + trace pointer on its own handle (the region-keyed cross-thread backstop cannot fire). initial-exec TLS + malloc-free handler + SIGTRAP arm-refcount discipline required.

nodes.label: WEAK fidelity tier — single-step L3 DESCEND_ALL
nodes.rationale: §Z1.1 LANDED. Cheapest complete end-to-end empty-ctor demo on any x86-64 Linux, native leaf only. Absolute-RIP bounded ring (overflow→truncated) rendered via render_versioned against a self pid==0 codeimage. Managed windows route to the §D3 stealth helper (single-step is unsafe against live managed code). Guards (deny-region/budget/watchdog) later ported onto the in-process path.

nodes.label: STRONG fidelity tier — Intel PT recorder-backed whole-window
nodes.rationale: §Z1.2. The out-of-band tier that makes the empty ctor faithful AND quiet: per-thread perf AUX event, no region; read_recorder→asmtest_pt_read_codeimage serves version-live bytes; not trusted until §Z2's synthetic fixture is green. SILICON-VALIDATED 2026-07-21 (hwtrace-pt-live 631/631 x4 on bare-metal PT). Intel bare-metal + paranoid<0/CAP_PERFMON; self-skips on AMD/ARM/VM/Docker.

nodes.label: CEILING fidelity tier — AMD LBR sampled hot-method survey
nodes.rationale: §Z1.3 LANDED but as a SAMPLED survey (asmtest_hwtrace_sample_window_amd), not the exact ~16-branch tail designed — exact whole-window on AMD is a hardware dead end (16-deep stack + throttle). Zen 4+ bare metal + CAP_PERFMON; survives managed code in-process (no TF/SIGTRAP). Zen 2 → EOPNOTSUPP → falls through to §D3 stepper via CEILING_FREE.
nodes.norm_label: ceiling fidelity tier — amd lbr sampled hot-method survey

nodes.label: Win64 capture trampoline (src/capture_win64.asm, eight variants)
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 DONE. Mirrors the eight asm_call_capture* variants for the MS x64 ABI: args rcx/rdx/r8/r9, 32-byte shadow space, FP xmm0–3 positional, callee-saved adds rdi/rsi + xmm6–15 (saved/seeded/captured/restored). Verified 21/21 both lanes (ms_abi native + real PE under Wine). Bigstruct passed by reference (simpler than SysV).

nodes.label: Win64 regs_t layout branch + manifest (LLP64-correct)
nodes.rationale: Phase 2 DONE. Third regs_t branch in include/asmtest.h (ASMTEST_ABI_WIN64, selected before __x86_64__): rdi/rsi added, LLP64 unsigned long long fields, ASMTEST_STATIC_ASSERT pins on every offset (size 352), new SENTINEL_RDI/_RSI. make manifest-win64 emits asmtest_abi_win64.json. Header is the single source of truth (tests/win64/win64_regs.h deleted).

nodes.label: Win32 runner port (src/platform_win32.c)
nodes.rationale: Phase 4 DONE (past the gate by request). Brings framework isolation to Win64: fork/waitpid→CreateProcess+WaitForSingleObject+TerminateProcess; mmap+PROT_NONE→VirtualAlloc+PAGE_NOACCESS; poll pool→WaitForMultipleObjects; sigaction+siglongjmp→vectored exception handler+__builtin_longjmp (no SEH unwind); fnmatch→portable glob_match. src/asmtest.c builds as the Win64 runner itself; MinGW emulated-fork rejected.

nodes.label: Phase 3 decision gate — ship --no-fork tier, defer Phase 4
nodes.rationale: Recommendation: stop at Phase 3. The --no-fork tier already delivers the substantive value (MS x64 ABI, capture, ABI-preservation on real silicon + real PE, drift-proofed, CI'd, no Windows host). Phase 4 buys only process-level isolation/timeout/guard pages (~1–2 weeks vs narrow benefit). Three lanes: A ms_abi native (fast feedback), B Docker+Wine (the tier proper), C windows-latest (optional sign-off vs Wine edge-case fidelity).
nodes.norm_label: phase 3 decision gate — ship --no-fork tier, defer phase 4

nodes.label: IBS-Op capture engine (include/asmtest_ibs.h, src/ibs_backend.c)
nodes.rationale: A separate producer, not an asmtest_trace_backend_t member (avoids the ~10-binding ABI churn). perf_event_open on ibs_op with swfilt+exclude_kernel; branch source reg[1]/target reg[7]/data reg[2] decode; asmtest_ibs_decode_op is a pure host-testable function (CI everywhere). survey_pid (one tid) + survey_process (all tids, one event+mmap per tid, capped IBS_MAX_CHANS=512). Phase-5 knobs shipped as a flags bitmask, not the sketched named fields.

nodes.label: asmspy --sample view + TUI mode 7 (Hot edges)
nodes.rationale: Phase 3 flagship, LANDED. asmspy_engine_sample drives asmtest_ibs_survey_process out of band (no ptrace, no single-step) and resolves both edge endpoints via asmspy_resolve (ELF symtab → JIT perf-map) so managed frames are named. The only rich TUI/headless view safe on a JIT — the exact case single-step views risk crashing. Verified live naming hot_spin's back-edge on Zen 2 without perturbing the target.

nodes.label: IBS statistical invariant — never feeds the parity cascade
nodes.rationale: IBS is statistical and must never feed the exact insns[]/blocks[] parity contract — a separate diagnostic producer, not a fidelity-cascade rung. Phase 4's sample_window_amd fallback flags fidelity=STATISTICAL and stays OUT of asmtest_trace_call_auto's exact cascade. Disclosed limits: races thread creation, throttle-bounded density, retired-op tagging quirks.
nodes.norm_label: ibs statistical invariant — never feeds the parity cascade

nodes.label: Trap-Flag stepper (src/ss_backend.c, ASMTEST_HWTRACE_SINGLESTEP)
nodes.rationale: Phases 0–4 LANDED. begin sets EFLAGS.TF; each #DB delivered as SIGTRAP, handler reads RIP, re-asserts TF, records conditionally (in-region only — callees stepped-not-recorded). Blocks derived from fall-through discontinuity via Capstone length-decoder. No perf/CAP_PERFMON/decoder library. Selected by enum behind the unchanged asmtest_hwtrace_* API, so all ten bindings get it free — first hardware-tier test that runs LIVE on the Zen 2 CI host.

nodes.label: Out-of-process ptrace tracer (W2, src/ptrace_backend.c)
nodes.rationale: Phase 5 W2 LANDED (x86-64 + AArch64). trace_call (own tracee) / trace_attached (foreign externally-attached pid, reads bytes via process_vm_readv) / _versioned / run_to (software int3 or hardware DR0/DR7 breakpoint for W^X JIT text). Call-depth aware (runs helper calls to their return at native speed). Region resolvers (/proc/maps, perf-map) + binary jitdump reader + time-aware codeimage recorder. Six live real-JIT lanes (V8/CoreCLR/HotSpot × perf-map+jitdump).

nodes.label: BTF branch-granular block-step (W3, src/ss_btf.c / PTRACE_SINGLEBLOCK)
nodes.rationale: DEBUGCTL.BTF=1 + TF=1 traps only on taken branches (one fault per branch, no 16-entry ceiling). Out-of-process form shipped as asmtest_ptrace_trace_call_blockstep/_attached_blockstep on x86 behind a hang-proof probe (some hypervisors mask DEBUGCTL.BTF and silently degrade). In-process form landed as a raw-MSR pinned-envelope tier (asmtest_ss_btf_trace) with per-trap re-arm + faithful truncation on any observed context switch.

nodes.label: Single-step operating envelope — exact-slow, small routines only
nodes.rationale: The trade is exact-cheap (trace ring) vs exact-slow (a fault per instruction) — NOT exact vs nothing. No depth ceiling; every retired instruction observed. But one kernel round-trip per instruction (~2.3µs/insn on Linux, ~6x on Windows), so it is the exact/zero-dependency/unprivileged backend for small registered routines, not whole programs or hot loops (that is the DynamoRIO tier's job). Complementary, not competing.
nodes.norm_label: single-step operating envelope — exact-slow, small routines only

nodes.label: hw.yml self-hosted workflow + HW_RUNNER_* variable guards
nodes.rationale: Security decision: self-hosted jobs live in a SEPARATE workflow with no pull_request/pull_request_target trigger (only workflow_dispatch + nightly schedule on main), environment: hw-runners approval gate, permissions: contents:read + no secrets. Each job is if: vars.HW_RUNNER_<LANE>=='1' && actor==owner, so it skips instantly (green with zero runners). Ephemeral JIT re-registration loop (runner-jit-loop.sh) de-registers after one job.

Only hardware + credentials are legitimate self-skip gates.

nodes.label: .asmtrace NDJSON schema (envelope, mandatory provenance, event kinds)
nodes.rationale: NDJSON: line 1 header {asmtrace:1,container,producer,provenance,arch}; each later line one event keyed by 'k'. Provenance mandatory {backend,exact,trust,window?,skip?,redacted?} — statistical streams MUST set exact:false. v1 kinds: trace/coverage/syscall/stream/call/graph/topo/survey/watch/df_step/df_edge/regstate/result/note/stitch/end. Reserved kinds are additive registry rows (ignore-unknown). Fidelity enforced BY the format: provenance mandatory, truncation/drop/redaction are fields not renderer discipline. Determinism: fixed field order, omit ts/pid/cmd. Draft until the Phase-3 freeze.
nodes.norm_label: .asmtrace ndjson schema (envelope, mandatory provenance, event kinds)

nodes.label: Shared NDJSON writer TU (cli/asmtrace_ndjson.c, asmtrace_emit)
nodes.rationale: One tested writer both asmspy --record and the Author-mode recorder link, so field order (and byte stability) has exactly one owner. Pure C11 + stdio (no ptrace/ncurses/Capstone). Header line + per-kind emit + end footer + JSON escaping; a writer closed without asmtrace_close leaves a TORN recording (deliberate, no atexit magic — a crash mid-record must be visible).

nodes.label: Golden .asmtrace corpus + low-fidelity fixtures (D6/D7)
nodes.rationale: tests/golden-asmtrace/: flat per-routine recordings from the deterministic emulator L0 producer (make asmtrace-golden, docker-cli authoritative on pinned Capstone 5.0.1), plus hand-authored never-regenerated low-fidelity/ fixtures (truncated, dropped, redacted, torn) each opening with a note event. The byte-stability check the whole sibling set replays.

nodes.label: vec512_t ABI-manifest row (scripts/gen-manifest.c)
nodes.rationale: Closes the named state-descriptor precondition: vec512_t (AVX-512 wide-vector capture) was absent from the ABI manifest though the type exists. A descriptor id names a struct row of asmtest_abi.json; the regstate event kind references a descriptor, never a register list. asmtest_abi.json is generated not committed, so the gen-manifest.c block is the whole commit.

nodes.label: asmtrace_export tool (speedscope / Chrome-Perfetto / lcov / DOT)
nodes.rationale: Dependency-free C11 tool (tools/asmtrace_export.c, libc only): NDJSON reader + backends. --speedscope evented profile (enter-only streams → open/close pairs via a shadow stack; time axis = per-tid event ordinal, unit:none — producers record no timestamps); --chrome B/E + heat counters; --lcov block offsets; --dot-tree. Refuses to export survey events as stacks (exit 2 + reason); refuses zstd container by magic.

nodes.label: Backend-completeness readers + panel (desktop/src/data + views)
nodes.rationale: Tested C++17 readers (nlohmann/json, engine-free) load three committed sources — asmfeatures sweep, benchmarks/boxes/ records, perf-history.jsonl — into typed rows; a torn JSONL line is skipped and counted. The desktop table renders tier×backend×arch with skip_reason VERBATIM and trace_insns vs insns_truth (AMD-LBR plateau made loud as TRUNCATED). Row order = producer order, never re-sorted.

nodes.label: Recording/Workspace .asmtrace document model + NDJSON loader
nodes.rationale: asmdesk::Recording groups events by kind + mandatory provenance; Workspace is a set of them (plan D3: every view takes one or two). Loader rules: reject newer major by name; missing provenance or non-bool exact rejected; unparseable non-final line is a hard error but a cut FINAL line ⇒ torn; no end footer ⇒ TORN; unknown kinds/fields load fine (forward compat). The D7 laws are executable, not prose.

nodes.rationale: D4/D9. asmtest-desktop links bundled Unicorn/Keystone engines → GPL-2.0 as a whole; asmtest-viewer is permissive + engine-free (ldd shows no libunicorn/keystone/capstone — the enforced gate). $(FRAMEWORK_OBJS) is NOT linked (asmtest.o defines its own main() colliding with main.cpp); five self-contained engine objects carry the GPL linkage. Doors render disabled-with-reason in the viewer (greyed-shows-why law D2).

nodes.label: Trace canvas view (per-offset heat + block gutter + disasm)
nodes.rationale: Pure view-model builder + thin ImGui draw. Rows = distinct offsets; heat = occurrences in the ordered insn stream; covered gutter = block membership (block-granular, never implies per-instruction coverage). HARD refusal (full-pane placard, no rows) on mixed basis tags — mixed bases mis-attribute every row. Loud never-collapsible TRUNCATED banner; heat from exact trace events only, statistical streams never folded in.

nodes.rationale: Per-step disasm/offset + value annotations + def-use in/out counts over recorded dataflow events, reusing asmspy_df_annotate/_defuse_counts/_loc_str verbatim (one annotation semantics for TUI and GUI). Reconstitutes an asmtest_valtrace_t VIEW by hand (no asmtest_valtrace_new engine symbol). Uses T1-based dt_rowstyle, not asmspy_df_rowstyle (which pulls the asmtest_slice_contains link dep).

nodes.label: Def-use slice explorer view (layered DAG, backward/forward cones)
nodes.rationale: The plan's crown jewel. Layered layout by step index, never force-directed (live force layouts are banned); edges greedily assigned the lowest free arc lane in ascending order → identical input yields identical layout. Click/router → backward + forward cones lit (T1 closures). Producer-agnostic (recorded edges: emulator L0 today, PT replay + live asmspy --serve later). Cones over a truncated stream are labelled lower bounds.
