nodes.label: Two-recording diff primitive (dt_diff, patient-zero alignment)
nodes.rationale: Plan D3: diff is a primitive, not a view feature, and is the Loom's patient-zero alignment seam (05 consumes dt_divergence — do not fork). Coverage union/delta, per-offset heat delta, hot-edge delta (kept statistical, never merged into exact heat), shared-prefix first divergence. Refuses on basis/arch mismatch. Routine identity CANNOT be checked in v1 (no code-bytes hash in the Envelope) — stated in identity_note, rendered as a first-class row rather than silently pretended.

nodes.label: Deep-link router + keyboard spine (nav.h, asmtrace-link:)
nodes.rationale: Plan D4's navigation spine: one internal API 'open recording R (optionally vs R') at step S / offset O in view V', used by every view + 06's test-failure producer + 08. Textual form asmtrace-link:v=&rec=&...; rec is a recording basename (schema carries no recording id); values percent-encoded. Every keyboard binding routes through dt_nav_go — no view-private navigation state.

nodes.label: Client-side slice closure library (desktop/src/analysis/slice.cpp)
nodes.rationale: Backward/forward closures over recorded defuse edges, semantics identical to src/dataflow.c's asmtest_slice_backward/_forward, zero engine deps (standard library only) so the render-only viewer never links libasmtest_dataflow (plan D5). O(V+E) per query vs the C slicer's O(V·E) — same result, matters at PT scale. Out-of-range origin yields the EMPTY slice, not {origin}. Parity checked against the C slicer over 200 LCG-seeded random graphs.

nodes.label: Finding #1 — leaked traced child on the fault path (High)
nodes.rationale: src/ptrace_backend.c:696. A traced routine taking a real signal (SIGSEGV/SIGILL) breaks the single-step loop with rc==OK, reaching normalize() without the kill(SIGKILL)/waitpid every other exit path performs (PTRACE_O_EXITKILL only fires when the tracer exits). Each faulting trace leaks a stopped unreaped child; a suite exhausts PIDs. FIXED d2c657c.
nodes.norm_label: finding #1 — leaked traced child on the fault path (high)

nodes.label: Finding #2 — RNG division-by-zero on wide ranges (High)
nodes.rationale: src/asmtest.c:585. asmtest_rng_range over a range wider than LONG_MAX makes hi-lo signed-overflow UB and (uint64_t)(hi-lo)+1 evaluates to 0 → % span is div-by-zero SIGFPE. Fix: compute span in unsigned and special-case the full range. FIXED f9e0ca4.

nodes.label: Finding #12 — README 'everything ships' oversells (Medium)
nodes.rationale: README.md:9 ('Every planned capability ships today') contradicts the rest of the docs: CoreSight never decodes on any host, Intel PT/AMD LBR self-skip off bare-metal hardware, AArch64 ptrace self-skips under qemu, eBPF codeimage self-skips without libbpf. Fix: split 'runs on any host' from 'compiles, self-skips off its hardware'. FIXED — reworded to 'implemented and exercised in CI'.

nodes.label: Finding S1 — release pipeline has never fired (High leverage)
nodes.rationale: git tag returns zero tags, yet CHANGELOG documents [1.0.0] and ~970 lines have accumulated under [Unreleased]. release.yml triggers on push tags v*, so its real path has only ever run as manual dispatch dry-runs. Recommend cutting a real tag — the fastest way to surface B2–B6 (missing Intel-mac payload, GPL source drift, token scope, checksum pinning) in practice rather than review.

nodes.label: 07-04 theme — 'green CI, broken artifact' cluster (D1/N1/N2/A1/A2)
nodes.rationale: The highest-value theme: several first-contact paths break with no gate catching it — D1 README authoring example won't assemble (ASM_FUNC used paren-form), N1 published Go module links a test-only fixture lib (-lasmtest_corpus, unconsumable), N2 Java jar compiled --enable-preview dead on JDK22+, A1 sigjmp_buf in the public header breaks -std=c11 consumers, A2 capture macros' compound literals fail from C++. All fixed 59adb74, each with a regression gate.

nodes.label: Finding C1 — asmspy Ctrl-C can leak a planted breakpoint into the target
nodes.rationale: Highest-value item. The TUI uses cbreak() not raw() and installs no SIGINT/SIGTERM handler, so Ctrl-C's default action terminates asmspy. If it lands during a software-int3 region trace, the planted 0xcc from rgn_plant_bp is not reverted — a POKETEXT byte is plain memory the kernel does not restore on tracer death, so the target later executes it and dies. The one hole in asmspy's 'never kill the target' invariant. FIXED 2026-07-21 (signal handler sets stop, engine's two-phase detach runs).

nodes.label: asmspy AArch64 support: single-step engine shim + NT_ARM_HW_WATCH watchpoints

nodes.label: In-line assembler silently drops unparseable statements (Keystone stat_count guard)
nodes.rationale: Core defect (not a binding defect): asmtest_assemble could return machine code MISSING an instruction the caller wrote, ok==true, empty err — a quiet wrong answer, worst shape for a library that asserts on machine code. Most reachable trigger: AT&T source assembled with the default Intel syntax (all ten bindings pass ASM_SYNTAX_INTEL by default). Keystone processes a recoverable-error statement and moves on: rc=0, ks_errno=OK, stat_count is the ONLY witness. T1 adds a red-by-construction regression test; T2 guards asmtest_assemble on a lower-bound count_statements/stmt_rules — the one choke point covers all ten bindings via the FFI (no ABI change). Measured dialect rules (three knobs): ';' separates in Intel/MASM/ATT/GAS but is a comment in NASM; '#' is a comment in x86 but an IMMEDIATE PREFIX in ARM (getting this wrong would have cost most ARM detection); string/char-literal + //, /* */ tracking needed. Over-counting is the safe direction (stat_count < expected can only fire on a genuine drop); false rejections are the failure mode that matters (T2-step4 sweep: 0 false rejections). Also caught: Keystone drops a whole unsupported-ISA source (APX) with KS_ERR_OK + 0 bytes. NO hardware/credential gate; Keystone pinned 0.9.2 (re-run probes on a bump). LANDED + independently re-verified 3/3.

nodes.rationale: Feature (RESOLVED 2026-07-22): a signal raised while DynamoRIO is attached on macOS was not delivered to the host runtime's handler (SIGILL under CPython / hang under pytest) — the one red path from the port's M2 bindings; un-skip test_drgate.py::test_signal_chaining. Root cause (single-threaded, confirmed by full runtime instrumentation of a debug fork build): the macOS 3-arg sigreturn needs a kernel-minted per-delivery validation token DR cannot forge for the signal frames it synthesizes; the real sigreturn was rejected and the thread resumed into DR gencode → ud2 → SIGILL → terminate. Fix (fork b8785a5d8): handle_sigreturn restores the app context via sigcontext_to_mcontext(DR_MC_ALL) and returns false to skip the real sigreturn (the VMX86 path) — no token needed. Tasks SC1-SC4. No hardware/credential gate (Intel-mac dev host + dispatch-gated drtrace-macos). Rich diagnostic trail: v1 multi-thread/i#58 framing REFUTED, v2/v3 superseded.
nodes.norm_label: macos dynamorio fork: fix signal chaining under attach (the drgate hang)

nodes.label: macOS out-of-process single-step via Mach exception ports
nodes.rationale: Feature: the macOS equivalent of the Linux out-of-process ptrace tracer — trace a routine or a foreign process's JIT method out of band via task_for_pid + an EXC_MASK_BREAKPOINT Mach exception port + thread_set_state to arm EFLAGS.TF, reconstructing the identical instruction/block stream. Mechanism decision up front: XNU cripples BSD ptrace PT_STEP (ENOTSUP unless addr==(caddr_t)1) forcing the Mach-SPI path; mirrors the five-symbol asmtest_ptrace_* API as asmtest_mach_* (new src/mach_backend.c + MIG mach_exc_server); run_to via int3 or DR7 hardware breakpoint. Tasks T1-T7. Gates: macOS x86-64 host (not containerizable — a host lane that self-skips off Darwin, not a skippable dependency); task_for_pid needs com.apple.security.cs.debugger (ad-hoc self-sign) or root → soft ASMTEST_MACH_EPERM self-skip; Apple Silicon arm64 out of scope.
nodes.norm_label: macos out-of-process single-step via mach exception ports

nodes.label: Managed whole-window: live compose, safe managed-arm routing, ambient PT stitching
nodes.rationale: Feature: three managed-runtime whole-window capabilities — (A) a live unwarmed .NET compose lane proving a method genuinely JIT'd + GC'd inside the window; (B) safe-managed routing so new AsmTrace() routes a managed window to PT where silicon exists else the §D3 out-of-process stepper, never in-process TF (opt-in ASMTEST_WHOLEWINDOW_SAFE_MANAGED, default byte-identical); (C) ambient AsyncLocal-driven per-thread PT hop stitching. Mechanism: JitMethodMap MethodLoadVerbose → codeimage track → close-time versioned decode; managed-runtime probe returns the distinct ASMTEST_HW_EMANAGED refusal sentinel; block-step the stealth window (~4-10x fewer stops); per-tid PT hop_open/hop_close (inherit=0, decode-at-disable). Tasks T1-T12. Gates: PT prongs need bare-metal Intel PT (self-skip); .NET is installable (dotnet-sdk-8.0 image, never self-skip). One PT arm consumes substrate helpers.
nodes.norm_label: managed whole-window: live compose, safe managed-arm routing, ambient pt stitching

nodes.label: Native trace-point to IL/bytecode/source-line attribution
nodes.rationale: Feature: resolve a captured native offset to file:line, a .NET IL offset, or a JVM bytecode index — ingest three existing feeds cheapest-first (jitdump JIT_CODE_DEBUG_INFO records the reader currently skips; CoreCLR MethodILToNativeMap event id 190 keyword 0x20000; HotSpot JVMTI CompiledMethodLoad addr→bci). Mechanism: asmtest_jitdump_debug_find + emu_line_map bridge; backend-neutral asmtest_srcmap schema (kind ∈ {source-line, IL-offset, bci}); version-keyed asmtest_srcreg on the codeimage capture sequence; .NET IlToNativeMap EventListener; in-tree JVMTI bci agent. Tasks T1-T7. No hardware/credential gate — every lane runs under plain docker (ptrace of own child). Enclosing-point granularity ceiling; JIT-compiled code only (interpreters out of scope); enablement asymmetry documented not engineered around.

nodes.label: Shared perf-AUX intel_pt helpers (pt_aux_open) — the one PT arm
nodes.rationale: The single Intel PT arm (doc-set position 9): pt_aux_open(pid, data_size, aux_size, aux_watermark, snapshot, out) + pt_aux_stop/pt_aux_close, extracted in substrate T1 and parameterized on pid and aux_watermark so foreign-pid attach, managed per-tid hops, and the F5 replay tier all consume it — any second perf_event_open on the intel_pt PMU outside these helpers is rejected in review.
nodes.norm_label: shared perf-aux intel_pt helpers (pt_aux_open) — the one pt arm

nodes.label: asmtest_pt_decode_window — the single libipt code-image-backed decode entry
nodes.rationale: Decodes a linearized AUX blob against a temporal code-image recorder (pt_image_set_callback), recording offsets from the first decoded IP (base_ip_out added by substrate T2, a source-incompatible change coordinated across the PT docs). CI-testable without PT hardware via asmtest_pt_encode_fixture. Self-trace caller = begin/end_window (substrate); foreign caller = attach_end (attach doc); its decoded offset stream is the executed path the F5 Unicorn replay consumes.
nodes.norm_label: asmtest_pt_decode_window — the single libipt code-image-backed decode entry

nodes.label: asmtest_codeimage — time-aware code-image recorder (bytes live at a capture sequence)
nodes.rationale: Landed substrate: asmtest_codeimage_new(pid) (0=self; foreign via soft-dirty/PAGEMAP_SCAN + process_vm_readv), track/refresh/now/bytes_at supplying the exact bytes live at each trace position (the write-after-protect race guard). Shared temporal-bytes source for PT decode (self + foreign), the F5 replay, the managed trackBytes labelling, and the version-keyed IL/bci attribution registry — gated by asmtest_codeimage_available (self-skip where soft-dirty absent).
nodes.norm_label: asmtest_codeimage — time-aware code-image recorder (bytes live at a capture sequence)

nodes.label: wilvk/dynamorio pinned fork + scripts/build-dynamorio-macos.sh → libdynamorio.dylib
nodes.rationale: Pinned DynamoRIO source fork (branch asmtest/macos-fixes) built reproducibly on macOS x86-64 via scripts/build-dynamorio-macos.sh; pin = fork commit + submodule SHAs recorded in third-party-digests.txt. Carries the macOS-scoped fixes (KERN_PROCARGS2 exec-path read, our_environ via _NSGetEnviron, chained-fixups export-trie parse, sigreturn context restore) that the port and signal-chaining docs land, and is consumed as DYNAMORIO_HOME by the drtrace tier and the nightly drtrace-macos CI job.

nodes.label: libdft64 differential taint oracle (PIN-4)
nodes.rationale: Second, independently-implemented byte-level taint engine (libdft64 on Intel Pin) that cross-validates the shipped DynamoRIO in-band taint client; make docker-taint-oracle diffs the two sink sets and classifies every divergence (DR bug / libdft gap / modelling difference).

nodes.label: Pin probe-mode arg/return capture (PIN-3)
nodes.rationale: Captures SysV int/FP arg registers at entry and return regs+flags at exit for a routine at native speed via Pin probe mode (jump-splice, no code cache); cross-checked against the out-of-process ptrace read_pc_ret path.

nodes.label: Intel SDE future/absent-ISA test lane (PIN-1)
nodes.rationale: Runs unmodified suite binaries under sde64 -future so ISA extensions the host CPU lacks (APX, AVX10.2, AMX, AVX-512-on-AVX2) get the full register/flag/memory/ABI battery on any x86-64 host; needs no future silicon (that is the point).

nodes.label: XED-decoded Pin trace tier + shared pintool substrate (PIN-2)
nodes.rationale: Pin decodes with XED (Intel's canonical decoder) so it can DBI-trace APX today where DynamoRIO's decoder aborts (DR #6226 open); sole author of the shared Pin substrate reused by PIN-3/PIN-4; asserts three-way offset parity Pin==DR==single-step.
nodes.norm_label: xed-decoded pin trace tier + shared pintool substrate (pin-2)

nodes.label: ptrace block-step reconstructor & tracer correctness + IBS pre-cover
nodes.rationale: Fixes silent defects in the ptrace block-step reconstructors (app int3, rep-prefix under-record, re-entrant step-over) and wires the shipped IBS covered-block set into the block-step fallback as a decode memoization; all edits in src/ptrace_backend.c.
nodes.norm_label: ptrace block-step reconstructor & tracer correctness + ibs pre-cover

nodes.label: Native RISC-V (rv64) host tier
nodes.rationale: Adds the RV64GC/LP64D native capture tier (regs_t branch, capture.s trampolines, example bodies, riscv64 Docker/binfmt lane) so asm-test runs ON a RISC-V machine, not only as an emulator guest.

nodes.label: Zero-config scoped tracing hardening
nodes.rationale: Ports the out-of-process descent guards (deny regions, instruction budget, ITIMER_REAL/SIGALRM watchdog) onto the in-process whole-window single-step path, closes drafted-but-unbuilt hygiene assertions, and lands doc-tail bullets; pure software, x86-64 Linux validation only.

nodes.label: AMD review follow-ups round 2 (2026-07-20 findings)
nodes.rationale: Actions a re-audit of HEAD's AMD surface: one real OOM fidelity defect (T1), a doc-drift cluster (T2), minor cleanups (T3), a trace_auto MSR-rung consistency nit (T4), diagnostics extension (T5), and the silicon/credential-gated self-hosted Zen runner (T6).

nodes.label: AMD native tracing: LBR backend + improvement roadmap
nodes.rationale: Single home for AMD-specific hardware-assisted native tracing: the shipped LBR snapshot backend (Part I), cross-checked improvement analysis (Part II), and the buildable improvement phases (Part III); all landed except Phase 6 (BRS period-adjust), hardware-blocked on Zen 3.
nodes.norm_label: amd native tracing: lbr backend + improvement roadmap

nodes.label: Shared Pin substrate (fetch-pin.sh, Dockerfile.pintool, docker-pintool)
nodes.rationale: Authored once by PIN-2 (fetch script + digest + license in T1, Dockerfile + lane in T2), reused by PIN-3 and PIN-4; env-keyed on PIN_VERSION/PIN_URL so one script serves both the 4.2 and 3.20 kits; Pin is proprietary freeware, test-lane only, never linked into libasmtest or any binding.

nodes.label: Pin 4.2 kit (4.2-99776-g21d818fa2), digest-gated
nodes.rationale: Newest Pin kit, self-computed SHA-256 (Intel publishes no official hash); bundles XED v2026.02.17 which decodes APX; Intel Simplified Software License (binary-only, no modification/RE); x86-64 gcc-linux only, so pintool lanes self-skip on non-x86 / non-Linux.

nodes.label: APX fixture: Pin traces, DR decoder-errors (PIN-2 T8)
nodes.rationale: Negative control proving the tier earns its keep: an APX/REX2 routine is XED-decoded on any x86-64 (ungated assertion) and traced end-to-end by Pin only on APX silicon (CPUID leaf7 subleaf1 APX_F hardware gate); DR replay of the same bytes must fail the completeness check while pinned DR predates APX.
nodes.norm_label: apx fixture: pin traces, dr decoder-errors (pin-2 t8)

nodes.label: Pin 3.20 kit (3.20-98437-gf02b61307)
nodes.rationale: libdft64's only tested Pin kit; its 2021 XED has no APX so it conflicts with PIN-2's 4.2 kit — both are pinned as distinct manifest rows and fetched by the same shared fetch-pin.sh with a no-'external' PIN_URL override.

nodes.label: libdft64 (AngoraFuzzer @ 20804d5) taint engine
nodes.rationale: Canonical byte-level Pin taint engine used as the oracle; documented coverage gaps (ignores eflags, no ZMM/AVX-512 tag slot, x87/FPU and ternary on TODO, XMM/YMM rules unverified) are enumerated as distinct named skips (libdft-gap-*/libdft-partial-*), never a silent pass.

nodes.label: Probe-mode entry/exit capture Pintool + refusal skips
nodes.rationale: Splices probes at a function's first bytes to capture args/return+flags at native speed and up to a 4KiB pointed-to buffer (validated via PIN_SafeCopy, never trusts a pointer); a function too short / non-relocatable is a per-target skip with a synthesized reason (Pin exposes no refusal reason-code API).
nodes.norm_label: probe-mode entry/exit capture pintool + refusal skips

nodes.label: Intel SDE 10.8.0 emulation lane
nodes.rationale: Whole-process emulation of future/absent ISA; transparency null test proves byte-for-byte identity to native for correct baseline code, plus an APX suite and the AVX-512-on-AVX2 un-skip; no CPU-feature self-skip ever added (needing no silicon is the lane's point); x86-only host, test/oracle-only, never shipped.

nodes.label: Application int3 SIGTRAP classification (bs_sigtrap_is_app)
nodes.rationale: An app int3 (JVM safepoint / .NET breakpoint) was misclassified as the tracer's own #DB, recording never-executed instructions as complete; fix classifies via the measured SI_KERNEL/TRAP_HWBKPT app-whitelist and forwards the signal via PTRACE_CONT — never PTRACE_SINGLESTEP/SINGLEBLOCK with SIGTRAP attached (measured fatal).

nodes.label: rep-prefix fidelity in block-step reconstructors
nodes.rationale: A rep-prefixed string op retires N times under TF single-step but appears once in block-step; instead of silently diverging the block-step path records it once and sets truncated, bounding the byte-identical promise honestly.

nodes.label: SP-aware call-out step-over (review #19 fix)
nodes.rationale: run_until resumes only when the return-address breakpoint is hit at the matching stack depth (PC==ret && SP==expected), so a stepped-over helper that re-enters the region at a deeper SP no longer hijacks the trace.

nodes.label: IBS block-step pre-cover memoization (asmtest_bs_precover)
nodes.rationale: A covered-block set from asmtest_ibs_normalize_blocks pre-decodes hot leaders once so the block-step drivers skip the per-stop Capstone re-scan on hits; statistical coverage may only memoize decode, never skip recording (IBS invariant) — output proven byte-identical to the uncached walk.

nodes.label: rv64 (RV64GC/LP64D) native host tier
nodes.rationale: regs_t branch, ABI checker (s0-s11 + fs0-fs11), capture.s LP64D trampolines, cycle counter via rdtime; fidelity gates in-tier: RISC-V has no condition-flags register so ASMTEST_NO_FLAGS makes ASSERT_FLAG_* a compile error, and no 128-bit vector capture so ASM_VCALL* self-skips with a printed ISA reason.

nodes.label: riscv64 Docker/binfmt CI lane (tonistiigi/binfmt)
nodes.rationale: make docker-riscv64 + a CI leg run the core suites under QEMU binfmt (~10-20x slower); per CLAUDE.md the binfmt/QEMU dependency is installable (added, pinned by tag@sha256) — NOT a hardware gate, so no self-skip is predicated on 'no RISC-V hardware'; qemu-user cannot emulate a ptrace tracer/tracee pair, so tracing tiers stay unported.

nodes.label: Guarded hw.yml self-hosted workflow
nodes.rationale: Carries every self-hosted job variable-guarded off (HW_RUNNER_* == '1') so it merges with zero hardware and each lane lights up by flipping one repo variable; deliberately no push/pull_request trigger (dispatch + nightly schedule only) so fork code can never reach the runner; environment: hw-runners + permissions: contents: read; ephemeral runners only.

nodes.label: AMD Zen live-capture lane (hwtrace-privileged-zen)
nodes.rationale: Runs make docker-hwtrace-privileged on real Zen silicon and FAILS if the AMD live paths self-skip (anti-vacuous-green assert); a non-escalating call_auto on a 25-back-edge loop is a regression signal, not a known finding. Hardware gate: a physical AMD Zen 4/5 Linux box + repo-admin flip of HW_RUNNER_AMD_ZEN; CAP_PERFMON alone suffices (measured, bypasses paranoid=4).

nodes.label: Bare-metal Intel PT lane (hwtrace-pt-baremetal)
nodes.rationale: The allowed-to-be-absent bare-metal PT job; self-skip-proof once the ASMTEST_REQUIRE_PT=1 require-mode target landed. Hardware gate: a bare-metal Intel PT x86-64 box (intel_pt PMU visible in-container under CAP_PERFMON). Registered + standing runner deployed 2026-07-23 (green runs recorded).

nodes.label: Runner registration + security-posture runbook (T1)
nodes.rationale: docs/internal/ci/runners.md: pinned runner tarball + SHA-256, ephemeral/JIT re-registration loop, label scheme, dedicated non-sudo runner user on CI-only boxes. Credential gate: repo-admin for registration tokens (expire after 1h), environments, and fork-PR settings.

nodes.label: Whole-window SIGTRAP guards (deny / budget / watchdog)
nodes.rationale: Adds a per-frame instruction budget, a process-global deny-region table, and an ITIMER_REAL/SIGALRM (no SA_RESTART) watchdog to ss_on_sigtrap's whole-window branch so a window that reaches a blocking libc call is bounded in wall-clock time; each guard firing stops TF re-assertion and reports truncated, all additions async-signal-safe (no malloc/lock/syscall in the handler).

nodes.label: IBS export OOM fidelity fix (T1, landed 2026-07-23)
nodes.rationale: eh_export/fh_export return -1 on calloc OOM but the four branch-stack lanes discarded it and returned OK, so an OOM'd export reported a complete empty survey (n==0) with no loss tell; fix captures the return and returns EUNAVAIL, proven by a fault-injected test (the path no test reached is why it shipped).
nodes.norm_label: ibs export oom fidelity fix (t1, landed 2026-07-23)

nodes.label: Self-hosted Zen runner (T6, infra-gated)
nodes.rationale: The one item the project cannot complete unaided: registering Zen 4/5 silicon under the already-built hw.yml hwtrace-privileged-zen lane. Gate: registered AMD Zen 4/5 hardware + a repo admin flipping HW_RUNNER_AMD_ZEN=1 (privileged capture, maintainer-only). Its one-shot leg ran green 2026-07-22 via self-hosted-ci-runners T3.

nodes.label: Governing constraint: AMD has no continuous trace; 16-entry silicon ceiling
nodes.rationale: Confirmed vs kernel sources, AMD APM/PPR, and LWN: AMD ships no Intel-PT/CoreSight-ETM equivalent and no BTS-to-memory through Zen 5; its branch-record facility is a fixed 16-entry stack captured into a perf sample. So on AMD you can match PT on completeness OR on near-zero overhead, not both — the Tier A / Tier B split follows from this.
nodes.norm_label: governing constraint: amd has no continuous trace; 16-entry silicon ceiling

nodes.label: Tier A: within-16-branch LBR snapshot (exact, low overhead)
nodes.rationale: A single branch-stack snapshot holds all taken branches of a small routine, reconstructing bit-for-bit identical insns[]/blocks[] to PT/DR/Unicorn; the shipped Part I backend (src/amd_backend.c asmtest_amd_decode). Live-verified on Zen 5; capture self-skips on Zen 2 (no branch facility), non-AMD, VMs, and default CI sandbox.
nodes.norm_label: tier a: within-16-branch lbr snapshot (exact, low overhead)

nodes.label: Tier B: LBR stitching (complete, higher overhead)
nodes.rationale: Splices overlapping 16-entry stacks sampled at every taken branch (sample_period=1) into one gapless sequence past the window; host-validated by test_amd_stitch and live-wired on Zen 5, complete only for runs whose taken-branch count fits the perf ring and survives throttling, else stitches as far as it can and flags loss (DynamoRIO is the whole-program answer).
nodes.norm_label: tier b: lbr stitching (complete, higher overhead)

nodes.label: BTF block-step tier (PTRACE_SINGLEBLOCK)
nodes.rationale: Headline correction: PTRACE_SINGLEBLOCK IS wired on mainline x86 (arch/x86/kernel/step.c) — the single-step plan's 'unwired' claim was wrong. One #DB per taken branch (~per block), the only exact real-CPU option on Zen 2, rootless (no CAP_PERFMON); complete-at-moderate-overhead, positioned above per-insn single-step and below DynamoRIO. Landed as Phase 2 in src/ptrace_backend.c.

nodes.label: Software-event/eBPF LBR boundary snapshot (branchsnap)
nodes.rationale: bpf_get_branch_snapshot reads the frozen 16-entry LbrExtV2 stack deterministically at the region boundary (HW execution breakpoint triggers a SEC(perf_event) BPF prog), fixing the two live Zen-5 failure modes (tiny routine too-fast-to-sample; post-glue window contamination). Default-on multi-exit (one breakpoint per exit up to ASMTEST_AMD_MAX_EXITS==4). Gates: Zen 4/5 perfmon-v2, Linux >=6.10, CAP_PERFMON+CAP_BPF.

nodes.label: MSR-direct LBR snapshot + cascade rung (Phase 5/8)
nodes.rationale: Reads LbrExtV2 FROM/TO MSRs directly (/dev/cpu/N/msr) around the region for an exact Tier-A snapshot with zero interrupts; Phase 8 inserts it as an escalation rung in asmtest_trace_call_auto between the truncated fast tier and the ~1000x block-step tier, gated on asmtest_amd_msr_available() and skipped under CEILING_FREE. Caveat: an in-process second re-run (non-idempotent side effects double). Needs root/CAP_SYS_ADMIN + the msr module.

nodes.label: IBS-Op complementary coverage lane (Phase 7, superseded+landed)
nodes.rationale: The only hardware branch source on Zen 2, purely statistical (one tagged op per NMI) so it is a coverage-confirmer/hot-edge pre-cover, never an ordered complete path and never feeds the parity contract. Superseded+landed via zen2-ibs-tracing-plan (Phases 0-4): branch target arrives in the perf PERF_SAMPLE_RAW record so with the kernel swfilt bit the lane is user-only + unprivileged at paranoid=2 — no CAP_PERFMON, no MSR_AMD64_IBSBRTARGET read.

nodes.label: BRS period-adjust single-window capture (Phase 6, forward-look)
nodes.rationale: The one open item, HARDWARE-BLOCKED: BRS exists only on AMD Family 19h Zen 3, and neither dev box is one (Zen 5, Zen 2). amd_brs_hw_config rejects the generic sample_period=1 open, so BRS opens only with a fixed period >=17 on the raw 0xc4 event; must be a distinct Tier-A-only mode (a fixed period breaks the Tier-B stitch overlap). Not implemented per the house 'no untested hardware code' rule — sole reason the plan stays out of archive.

nodes.label: asmspy interactive process tracer
nodes.rationale: Out-of-band ncurses/headless ptrace tracer: 11 headless subcommands + 9 TUI modes over the ptrace attach seam; the CLI view family the desktop GUI extends.

nodes.label: asmspy --dataflow --auto targeting
nodes.rationale: Theme H: ranks the hottest IBS entry edge to auto-pick a running routine to trace with no operator symbol; a pure resolution-layer module over the sample engine, plus a bounded entry wait so no pick hangs.

nodes.label: .asmtrace recording format
nodes.rationale: The keystone contract: versioned NDJSON event log + JSON header with reserved event kinds, state descriptors, and mandatory provenance; every GUI view is a reader/writer of it.

nodes.label: the Loom (spacetime fabric)
nodes.rationale: Flagship interaction concept: a recorded run as a fabric of value worldlines, composing slice explorer + operand timeline + diff into one selectable object answering residency x route x place x intervention.

nodes.label: def-use slice explorer (crown jewel)
nodes.rationale: The differentiated def-use lineage view no other tool offers; two producers (emulator L0 + zero-perturbation PT replay), producer-agnostic, renderable from recorded defuse edges.

nodes.label: diff as a first-class primitive
nodes.rationale: One alignment engine over two .asmtrace recordings classifying divergence (value/address/control-flow/FP-env) — a design-level primitive, not a later feature.

nodes.label: navigation spine (dt_nav_go)
nodes.rationale: One deterministic router as the only navigation state; every deep link resolves through it, so most nav findings are a thin layer, not a rewrite — but the keyboard spine and back/forward are unwired.

nodes.label: graded fidelity chrome (severity)
nodes.rationale: Collapse proliferating fidelity chrome into one fixed vocabulary graded into 3 tiers via a new schema severity field, so integrity failures stop being buried among benign notes.

nodes.label: dockable workspace panes
nodes.rationale: Convert closeable tabs into real kPane* dockable panes Begin()'d under the names layout.cpp already docks — the structural keystone that unblocks shared selection, presets and wayfinding.

nodes.label: Intel PT trace backend
nodes.rationale: perf_event_open AUX capture + libipt instruction decode with branch-boundary block normalization; landed and silicon-validated on bare-metal Intel, self-skips everywhere else.

nodes.label: ARM CoreSight trace backend
nodes.rationale: ETM/ETE waypoint trace decoded by OpenCSD; the reconstruction core is host-validated, but the live OpenCSD decode tree stays board-gated (forward-look), the sole reason the plan stays active.

nodes.label: attach-to-foreign-JIT tracing (Phase 2)
nodes.rationale: Trace a running foreign JIT's generated code out of band via PT/ETM + a time-aware code-image; the Intel-PT half (foreign-pid capture + wiring) is DONE and silicon-validated, HV/EPT frontier remains research-grade.

nodes.label: time-aware code-image recorder
nodes.rationale: asmtest_codeimage: a timestamped cross-process code-image timeline (soft-dirty/PAGEMAP_SCAN + optional eBPF PROT_EXEC detector) so a branch-trace decoder gets the bytes live at each trace position under re-JIT/address reuse.

nodes.label: Track A — publish the bindings
nodes.rationale: Turn the ten packaging-scaffolded bindings into registry-installable packages with native libs bundled; pipeline was broken in four ways (fixed 2026-07-17), go-live now gated only on credentials.

nodes.label: Track C — Capstone disassembly in diagnostics
nodes.rationale: src/disasm.c annotates faults, traces, and uncovered blocks with instruction text across all four guests; optional/gated on Capstone, degrades to bare offsets.
nodes.norm_label: track c — capstone disassembly in diagnostics

nodes.label: Track D — wide-vector capture (AVX/AVX-512/SVE)
nodes.rationale: vec256/vec512/svec capture beyond 128 bits with CPUID/HWCAP self-skip; validated on real AVX-512 (Zen 5) and Neoverse-N2 SVE silicon across all ten bindings.

nodes.label: Track E — coverage-guided fuzzing & mutation
nodes.rationale: emu_fuzz_cover1 feeds emulator block coverage back into input generation; emu_mutation_test1 bit-flips a routine and scores the suite — both contained inside the emulator.

nodes.label: Track F — emulator invariant & watchpoint assertions
nodes.rationale: Mid-execution memory read/write watchpoints + block-entry register invariants + emu_snapshot/restore, catching corruption even when restored before return (x86-64 guest).
nodes.norm_label: track f — emulator invariant & watchpoint assertions

nodes.label: M0 DynamoRIO macOS attach go/no-go
nodes.rationale: The dominant unknown: whether in-process dr_app_* attach + Mach-O marker resolution work on macOS; blocked upstream for years then unblocked via a source fork, landing 13/13 on the Intel-mac dev host.

nodes.label: macOS clean-room install fidelity
nodes.rationale: Make an install-test prove the bundled native lib is the only thing that could satisfy a binding load — no leaked dev build/, Homebrew dylib, or DYLD override — across both Darwin arches.

nodes.label: Loom (glossary term)
nodes.rationale: Glossary definition of the desktop GUI's data-flow lineage tool that weaves def-use edges into a fabric of worldlines.

nodes.label: fabric (glossary term)
nodes.rationale: The woven 2-D field the Loom draws — lanes running left-to-right as time, worldlines threading through them (the def-use lineage graph over the step axis).

nodes.label: worldline (glossary term)
nodes.rationale: A single value's def-use timeline through the Loom's fabric — born at a definition, threading the steps that read it.

nodes.label: patch-bay (glossary term)
nodes.rationale: Desktop metaphor for tracer contention / capture-budget arbitration: only so many tracers can be plugged into so many targets at once.

nodes.label: patient-zero (glossary term)
nodes.rationale: The GUI's name for the first divergence between two recordings — the earliest step at which they stop agreeing.

nodes.label: born-untraced (glossary term)
nodes.rationale: A value the Loom shows entering computation from outside the traced window (an unrecorded upstream definition), drawn with a caution glyph.

nodes.label: Capstone (glossary term)
